on behalf of the alde group. madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i hope that we have arrived on the eve of the adoption of this pesticide package. the two compromise texts which will be put to the vote in this parliament seem to me to be balanced and worthy of support, and in several respects. the advances for producers and users are notable: simplification of authorisation procedures through, in particular, the division into three zones and the accompanying mutual recognition. i would have liked to have had just one area, to ensure even more coherence throughout the union, but the member states have been a little too cool. increased training requirements for both vendors and users - better knowledge and handling of pesticides - are a guarantee of better health protection, but also of economic gains. the advances for animal welfare advocates are also notable, particularly through the sharing of animal test data. the progress made in protecting health and the environment is very significant; in the long term, the most dangerous substances will be replaced by less harmful ones. i can't help but touch on the highly controversial issue of endocrine disruptors. until now, there was no definition. there was no legislation on this issue. the compromise gives the european commission four years to make scientifically based proposals for measures to define endocrine disrupting properties. this scientific definition will make it possible to classify products according to whether or not they are disruptive and will, in fact, provide the scientific legal framework for industry. the compromise text also takes account of the issue of bees and their indispensable role in the ecosystem. i think that the wording of the compromise attached to the european commission's statement is a major step forward. the effects of the active substances on the overall development of the bee, but also on nectar and pollen, shall be considered. i would like to reassure some stakeholders who have expressed doubts about the availability of active substances and products. this compromise takes into account their fears. the three-zone system ensures that member states can authorise a greater number of products. there is also a possibility of derogations. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the protection of the environment is based on the principle of the protection of the environment. there is also the review clause, which asks the european commission to analyse the impact of this legislation on the diversification and competitiveness of agriculture. finally, and most importantly, as my colleagues have pointed out, we are encouraging the manufacturers of pesticides to develop new products which are effective and respectful of human health and the environment. in conclusion, i would like to remind you that plant protection products are medicines for plants and should therefore only be used in a controlled and prudent manner. for the greens/efa group mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i would like to recall how in 1992, when the french vote for the maastricht treaty was in full debate, jacques delors spoke to the general assembly of the greens, who could move the missing 1 or 2%. he told us: "vote for the euro, then there will be political europe, because if political europe is not made to control europe, the peoples will not accept it, they will never accept it". he hadn't convinced us. the maastricht treaty had been signed, but political europe had not been achieved. and that's the problem we face today. why were we against the euro at that time? i would simply say that we really need to apply the good aspects of the maastricht treaty. we have a real problem with the definition of the exchange rate, as my predecessors have said many times. this exchange rate is allocated to the council, we must find ways of ensuring that the council sets a european exchange rate which is not the result of the european central bank's random choice of interest rates but is really the expression of an industrial policy. we must find the instruments. secondly, the central bank's objective is not only to have a rate close to 2%, but also to apply europe's policy, that is to say the lisbon-göteborg policy. we must have a policy of refinancing and re-calculating private debts by the central bank in accordance with the göteborg-lisbon principle. thirdly, as has already been said, there must be european supervision, and the central bank is best placed to carry it out.

in writing. i am well aware that the belder report is concerned solely with economic and trade relations with the western balkans and the obvious need for the european union to help with their reconstruction, both economically and legally, politically and socially. i am surprised, however, that despite the assertion that this aid, like the accession processes, must be differentiated and adapted to each country, it is not really taken into account in the report on the specific situations of each country. serbia, for example, is not even mentioned. and above all, this parliament, always so quick to denounce violations of human rights all over the world, or to call for 'human rights' clauses in its international cooperation agreements, succeeds in the feat of voting a report on the balkans without mentioning once the dramatic and unacceptable situation of the serb populations of kosovo, who have become pariahs on the historic land of their ancestors. but by welcoming the hundreds of millions of euros donated to the authorities who cause, organize or tolerate this situation.
in writing. ms grabrowska's report calls for a permanent dialogue between all the european institutions and civil society 'representatives' for policy-making and legislation at the european level, i.e. the mandatory and formalised organisation of participatory 'democracy' at eu level. the problem is that participatory 'democracy' is the fake nose of those who reject genuine democracy: it allows dialogue to be limited to the most activist organisations, which are rarely the most representative; it pretends to take the opinion of the citizens upstream, only to refuse to really consult them later. if the europe of brussels claims to want to listen to the citizens, let it take note of the french and dutch 'no's' to the european constitution and abandon the treaty of lisbon, which is only a copy of it. if, as the rapporteur suggests, opinion polls are to be taken into account, then the accession negotiations with turkey should be stopped, since the vast majority of european citizens are hostile to them. if the principle of decision-making as close as possible to the citizen is to be respected, europe must stop governing our daily lives. then she'll be credible when she talks about democracy.
in writing. we abstained on the weiler report on the protection of consumers and businesses against unfair practices and misleading advertising, because we are critical of its importance. the first is that european legislation on these subjects is in the form of directives, i.e. member states are relatively free in the means they use to achieve the objectives assigned to them. the rapporteur's wishes for the harmonisation of national legislation in both form and substance must remain wishes, unless they lead to unacceptable interference by the european union in the legal and administrative systems of the member states, without any real benefit for consumers. the second is that the main added value of the european union in these areas would be to help resolve crossborder disputes. the problem is not really solved in the texts in force or required. the main objective of such legislation should not be to exist for its own sake, but to protect consumers and businesses.
in writing. impact studies carried out by french institutes and technical centres show that the proposed revision of the european pesticide directive could lead to the disappearance of a large number of products currently available on the market. it is important that this project empowers farmers in the union to protect their crops. otherwise, production cuts for crop sectors would be very significant and could also have a significant impact on animal sectors. whole plant life could be condemned in france and europe and the very role of agriculture, which is to feed our fellow citizens with healthy and varied products, would be threatened. without compromising consumer and user protection, the new regulation must not jeopardise the diversity of chemical families and innovation. it must therefore immediately provide for alternative solutions. this is the only way to avoid the relocation of many agricultural products which provide jobs and wealth. in the face of all these crucial challenges for farmers, vegetable, fruit and cereal producers, it is important to continue to be vigilant about the reforms under way and the national implementing measures that will be taken.
in writing. with this text, which limits the production and marketing of pesticides, and the accompanying text, which regulates their use, europe is finally setting itself exemplary standards for pesticides. the report by mrs hiltrud breyer is indeed moving in the right direction. on the one hand, it allows the placing on the market of products which are not dangerous; it also bans 22 substances considered to be very harmful. if we are to have a world-wide, rational agriculture in the long run, we must welcome this advance by the european union. european agriculture, which uses plant protection products in abundance, will not be weakened. on the other hand, eu legislation is becoming more stringent in the fight against toxic pesticides with these texts.
in writing. what i take away from mrs gottardi's report on public finances is that it does not draw any lessons from the global crisis. mrs gottardi calls 'market failure' and 'a lack of supervision' what is in reality the failure of a system that has been imposed on us for decades: that of forced deregulation, of global ultra-trading, of the absurd financialization of the economy, of the market king supposed to self-regulate. it is not the partial replans decided upon vaguely at the g20 or in brussels that will fundamentally change the situation. it would require a re-examination of the economic dogmas to which we are still subject. the crisis has shown that the free movement of goods, services, capital and people leads not to prosperity but to catastrophe. it also proved that the nation state is the relevant and effective level of decision, action and reaction, even if nicolas sarkozy felt obliged to be accompanied everywhere by mr barroso to make believe that the european union was useful in this situation. in this context, the rapporteur's sound advice on public financial management and his call for respect for the stability pact are unfortunately of little use.
on behalf of the pse group. mr president, when the regulation establishing standards for security features and the inclusion of biometric features in european passports was adopted in 2004, member states did not provide for any derogation from the obligation to give fingerprints. however, current experience shows that existing technology does not yet ensure that the fingerprints of children under 12 years of age are sufficiently reliable to be used as a security element in passports. i therefore welcome the compromise reached with the member states to set an age limit of 12 years for the collection of biometric data, with a review clause in three years. and we have accepted the derogation for member states which have already adopted legislation for children over six years of age. the use of such data would only be acceptable if it actually protected our children. it's not yet. but we are also open to the possibility of positive developments in technology in this field. our priority is to ensure the safety of children traveling alone to prevent any kidnapping or trafficking of children. the inclusion of data in passports gives a false impression of security because it does not prevent a child from crossing a border without parental authorisation. the compromise reached with the member states will enable the commission to present a report on the requirements for minors travelling alone when crossing external borders. the report will thus make it possible to propose initiatives to ensure a european approach to the rules on the protection of minors when crossing the external borders of the member states. finally, biometric elements in passports should only be used to verify the authenticity of the document and the use of sensitive personal data such as biometric elements is only acceptable with strict rules on the protection of personal data.

madam president, sustainable fisheries management does indeed involve monitoring fishing effort, but it also requires taking account of the effort of fishermen. the fisheries sector, everyone agrees, especially deep sea fishing or deep sea fishing, is the most difficult in the world, even if we are no longer in the fishing conditions of the basques, the icelanders of the 19th century, who set out on long campaigns. the profession remains very tough and deserves respect with its 24,000 deaths annually. fisheries is the perfect example of global activity because of the globalisation of resources, that is, fish, which know no borders, so the standards can only be international. as it is a matter of international regulation of fishermen's work, the legislator is obviously the ilo and we are celebrating the 50th anniversary of the first ilo conventions on fishermen, on minimum age, on workplace control, on medical examination and on housing. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament. all this must of course be ratified as soon as possible, before 2012. it is a good example of the joint management of the common parts of the planetary co-ownership and it is an emergency because the professions of the sea, of dockers, of fishermen, of sailors, in today's global economic competition, are exposed to all the abuses, all the exploitations, all the trafficking, even all the situations of slavery, in the name of obviously reducing costs. legal protection is therefore imperative for health, housing, safety, working time, living conditions, wages, medical care and therefore employment contracts and social security. so we are creating a minimum legal status for the fisherman and in this respect we are leveling the playing field for global competition. this is not necessarily of interest to european fishermen who already have this, but for fishermen from the world, from peru, from asia or from africa, it is a great step forward.

in writing. the pretext for this directive on the opening up of public procurement to competition in the arms industry was the strengthening of the competitiveness of the european arms industry, which was supposed to be hampered by european markets that were too narrow and too closed in on themselves. it is true that the text proposed today has taken account of a number of problems raised by the commission's original text, such as its scope, the non-application of the wto agreement on public procurement, financial thresholds and confidentiality. but it is in line with the logic of brussels, which believes that no sector, even if it is strategic and vital, should escape its supervision, liberalization and privatization. it does not guarantee respect for the sovereignty of the member states, which are legally solely responsible for their national security. it does not promote the existence of large-scale markets in europe, where national defence budgets are being drastically reduced. it does not establish any community preference which alone would allow the natural emergence of a genuine european market. it reinforces the civil/military dichotomy, so specific to europe, and which has already cost us so much. and above all, it puts economic and market considerations above all else. these serious flaws in essential points have motivated our opposition.

i'm the reporter. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, our discussions on this second strategic energy analysis were of course marked by the new gas supply crisis between russia and ukraine. this crisis has exposed the weaknesses, the fragility of interconnections and the difficulty of the european union to react and speak with one voice. the crisis has revealed for the third time the need for a common energy policy. however, i must say - and our commissioner has just said this - that we are seeing progress and more cooperation and solidarity between member states, and therefore hope for a solution to manage these crises. i would like to thank the members who have contributed greatly to enriching this report, which we have been conducting with a bang, since we were informed of the communication in november. i shall not go into detail about everything we have said in this resolution, but perhaps i should like to give you an idea of the message that the committee on industry wanted to convey with this resolution. the context is as follows. the climate constraint will become more severe, the security of supply of the european union is threatened by increasingly serious and frequent crises and the competitiveness of the european union may be undermined. this implies the need to think differently about energy consumption and use in the european union, to think differently about our energy resources and to enable us to exploit the huge pool of jobs in the energy sector, jobs which are so crucial in the context of the economic crisis we are going through. what do we propose? the short term is to affirm the vision of three times 20 by 2020 of the energy-climate package and to transform it into a european energy policy. it is a combined action at several levels: global, european, national and local, which means that the first priority we have indicated is of course energy saving, energy efficiency and the development of renewable energies, because in this area the potential of the european union is considerable. in particular, the 20% energy efficiency target should be made binding. secondly, the security of supply of the european union should be improved through investment in networks and, in particular, interconnections. solidarity between states means that the networks must supply isolated regions which are heavily dependent on a single supplier. this also means that the gas security directive needs to be revised to become a european crisis management tool. improving security of supply also means strengthening and structuring the dialogue with transit and producer countries. we must develop these energy interdependence relations, particularly with russia and the mediterranean area. thirdly, having an internal market is a crucial element for security of supply. but how can one member state be supplied via another if interconnections are weak or non-existent? four of them are to identify best practice at international level. in this respect, let us increase trade with japan and the united states - particularly california - but let us not be fooled, our relations with these energy-consuming countries are based both on cooperation and also on competition, particularly in energy technologies. and then there's the long-term, which is very important. the aim is to plan the future of energy in the european union. we should be able to write the roadmaps for the supply of the european union in 2050 on the basis of scenarios for the period from, say, 2010 to 2020. this requires setting ambitious targets for the fight against climate change. our committee proposes to reduce co2 emissions by 60 to 80%, but perhaps by at least 80% tomorrow, to improve energy efficiency by 35% and to achieve a 60% share of renewable energy by 2050. our parliament is asking that this road map should include the evolution of the various sources of energy in order to plan investments in means of production, interconnections and research and development. in the energy mix for 2050, the industry committee confirmed the role of nuclear power alongside other energy sources, such as renewable energies, and the desire to develop energy storage facilities and to use the potential of the sun, whose resource is infinite.

the agenda calls for a brief presentation of the report by jürgen schröder, on behalf of the committee on development, on the impact of economic partnership agreements (epas) on development (2008/2170 (ini)) (a6-0513/2008).
member of the commission. − mr president, the commission welcomes the report by mr schroeder, which represents a balanced overview of the diversity of opinions surrounding the development impact of the economic partnership agreements (epas). the dossier continues to evolve. we have signed a full economic partnership agreement with the caribbean region, whilst we have negotiated interim agreements with countries and regions in africa and the pacific. these interim epas provide for a trade regime compatible with wto rules and preserve important trade preferences for these countries. the interim agreements are only transitory in nature, as they will be replaced by full regional epas. the pace of these negotiations will be set by the regions concerned to ensure those objectives and coverage match their own integration processes, capacity, needs and political priorities. in parallel, the programming of the 10th european development fund has moved on. most of the regional and national programmes are signed. in anticipation of the epas, these programmes include considerable support to help our african, caribbean and pacific (acp) partners make the most of the agreements: direct support for the implementation of the agreements and indirect support to build up infrastructure and productive capacity. the commission recognises the essential role of development finance. at the same time we welcome the fact that the report acknowledges that the development objectives and outcomes of the agreements are a much wider issue than just financial support. we also recognise the essential role of reform in the acp regions in reaching the development objectives, as set out in paragraph 14 of the report. this includes fiscal reform and changes to revenue systems. the reforms offset shifts in the tax base due to liberalisation and are in themselves valuable steps to ensuring sustainable public financing in the acp. another essential objective is to support regional economic integration in the acp. the interim agreements do not yet include all acp countries. this is exactly why these agreements are only temporary pending full agreement. the full agreements will be flexible and comprehensive. building up supply-side capacity to trade and engage in goods and service sectors underpins the economic value of a trade agreement. the commission’s view is that protectionism is never a valid policy option. however, we do acknowledge that protection – the legitimate use of measures to protect sensitive sectors and emerging industry – is a valid and essential policy tool. this is why the epas contain all sorts of flexibilities, and in particular exclusions and asymmetrical commitments for the acp side, as called for in the report. on the eu side, our markets are completely open for acp products, with increased cooperation to meet technical and health standards and facilitate trade. acp countries will only open their markets gradually, with the possibility to maintain exceptions. the commission does not see our commitment to the epa process ending on signature. this is the start of a process of enhanced dialogue, careful implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of the effect, especially as regards the development impact. all of this will use the institutions established to implement the agreement to ensure transparency and the participation of parliamentarians and civil society. the commission therefore welcomes the report by mr schröder and will provide a detailed reaction to the points raised in due course.
the point is closed. the vote will take place tomorrow. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
in writing. parliament will vote on thursday on mr schröder's report on the economic partnership agreements (epas). i would be extremely disappointed if the first expression of our institution on this subject, which is both very technical and highly political (since the whole future of our relations with the acp countries is at stake), were to end in the adoption of mr schröder's report. the pse will not vote on this text because it does not reflect the concerns of both europe and our acp partners about the epas and the way they are negotiated. the european parliament has tabled and will vote on a resolution which, contrary to the rapporteur's position, places development at the heart of the priorities of the epas, which rejects the liberalisation of public services and any negotiation on singapore issues or on services against the will of the acp countries, which promotes regional integration, which calls for massive financial support to upgrade the economies of the acp countries and which takes account of the specificities and fragility of these countries, whether ldcs or not. these are the conditions which would make epas acceptable. unfortunately, we are still a long way from that.
the agenda calls for a brief presentation of the report by mr gyula hegyi, on behalf of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, on the european nature reserves (2008/2210 (ini)) (a6-0478/2008).
member of the commission. − mr president, halting the loss of biodiversity is a priority for the union and for the commission. it is quite literally a question about the future of life on earth. but, despite the fundamental importance of preserving biodiversity, progress to date has been limited. in december 2008, the commission adopted the first comprehensive assessment of progress made at both european community and member state levels. despite the positive developments that have been made in recent years – for instance the natura 2000 network – the eu’s biodiversity is still under continuous pressure due to habitat destruction, pollution, climate change and the impact of invasive species. the commission’s conclusion was that we are highly unlikely to meet our 2010 target of halting biodiversity decline – and that further intensive efforts will be required, both at member state and eu levels. against this background, the commission welcomes the consistent support that parliament has given to efforts to protect europe’s rich and varied natural heritage. we greatly welcome the initiative of mr hegyi for producing this important resolution on wilderness in europe. i would like to start by making the general observation that many of the issues highlighted in the report are already being followed up by the commission. for example, in december 2008, the commission adopted a communication, ‘towards an eu strategy on invasive species’. we are also launching an overall reflection on the future of eu biodiversity policy and look forward to the input of the european parliament on these questions. issues such as improving implementation and the relationship between biodiversity and climate change must be explicitly considered. it is also important to add one clarification to the report. there is an ongoing assessment of the effectiveness of our nature legislation – the so-called article 17 reports – but there are currently no plans to amend our legislation, and the main focus is on more effective implementation. turning to the subject of wilderness, europe is densely populated and only 1-2% of the territory has not been affected by human intervention. but while these wilderness areas are small in area, they are of high value in both scientific and cultural terms. they can even, as is the case in the common trans-border national park of the german bavarian and czech bohemian forests, be a symbol for european cooperation and integration. most of these areas are already a part of the natura 2000 network. however, this report provides the inspiration to look again at the wild and nearly wild areas in the eu and to see if there are instances where additional european actions can help protect these special places. the commission has commissioned a number of studies and is cooperating with the czech eu presidency. a conference will take place in prague in may 2009. this conference will offer a platform to consider the issues related to wilderness areas in europe and identify measures needed to ensure their conservation. let me conclude by confirming that the commission recognises that europe’s landscape is the result of a long process of human intervention. the concept of a living landscape that balances the needs of nature with the needs of man is the basis of the thinking that underpins natura 2000. we certainly do not intend to re-convert our existing landscapes into wild nature, but we need to publicly commit ourselves to preserving the last remaining wild areas of europe. for this reason, the commission considers the european parliament resolution timely. it represents a very welcome input into the prague conference. thank you very much to the rapporteur.
we are of course glad to note your statement, but i would remind you that the use of rule 45 is in the hands of the conference of presidents and that in the conference of presidents votes are weighted, that is to say that the large groups, including yours, have a great deal of power to decide what should go to the plenary under one article or another. i am a little bit like you, i have to say that we may have gone from a phase of too much laxity to a phase of too much rigidity and that the truth is certainly somewhere in between. but we'll get the right people to follow, so don't worry. i would also like to ask you, ladies and gentlemen, to turn to your group chairmen. i think that's where your message will be best understood. the point is closed. the vote will take place tomorrow. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
the agenda calls for a brief presentation of the report by mr luís queiró, on behalf of the committee on transport and tourism, on an agenda for a sustainable future of general and business aviation (2008/2134 (ini)) (a6-0501/2008).
, member of the commission. − mr president, the commission welcomes the report and thanks the rapporteur and the committee for their excellent work. in january 2008 the commission for the first time published a communication on general and business aviation. this was followed by a very positive council conclusion in april 2008, and now by this important report of parliament. general and business aviation is an important sector of the eu aeronautical industry, worth about eur 2.3 billion annually. it invests substantially in research and development, and is growing fast. over two thirds of all aircraft certified in the eu are in this sector. general and business aviation mainly comprises small and medium-sized enterprises. it is also a very diversified sector. the regulations need to be adapted to this specific nature, without, however, compromising safety or security. we are happy to see that this notion of proportionality is encouraged by parliament in its report. there are three main areas on which we will have to focus our efforts in the nearest future: development of common eu safety standards for general aviation; integration of non-commercial aviation into the next generation of air traffic management (atm) systems for europe; and reducing the negative environmental footprint of the sector. the commission intends in the coming year to propose a number of eu implementing rules ensuring a uniform level of safety of non-commercial aviation. as highlighted in your report, we have to make sure that they are not only providing for an adequate level of safety, but are also proportionate and do not impose unnecessary burden on operators. we will also continue the development of the future atm system for europe with a clear understanding that airspace is a common good that should be accessible for all its users in a safe way. from the perspective of general aviation, the single european sky and sesar will be of the utmost importance for enhancing, in a safe way, access to airspace and aerodromes. these technologies will open the way to new services, as yet unseen in europe. last but not least, general and business aviation, despite the ongoing technological advances, are also impacting on the environment and, like the wider airline industry, they need to contribute to reducing these impacts. here as well, proportionality will be an important principle to follow. the commission is looking forward to working with parliament along the lines of the report, and will report back on the progress made.
the point is closed. the vote will take place tomorrow. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to congratulate our colleague, mr caudio fava, on the remarkable work he has done in recent months to produce a balanced text. the task was not easy, and the road was full of pitfalls. i would like to stress three points. the penalty here lies with the employer who is guilty, while the migrant is considered a victim. in addition to financial penalties, criminal sanctions are provided for in the event of repeated offences, trafficking in human beings or exploitation of minors. i think that these criminal sanctions are essential, and i think that we must also ensure that regular checks are carried out so that this directive can be effective. another positive point i would like to make is the automatic payment of arrears of wages to workers. finally, the interests of irregular workers are defended by associations and trade unions, so that they can denounce the employer without risking prosecution. of course, as is the case here with many other texts, we could have gone further, but can we take the risk of adopting a compromise position when this text already allows for serious progress in the protection of workers and their dignity? we must support a balanced approach to migration and recognise that labour immigration is more than necessary and will become even more so in the future given demographic projections. in this context, it is therefore essential to affirm that the model we want is one in which immigrant workers are recognized as full-fledged workers, enjoying the same rights as workers in the member states. it is therefore essential that we take action to defend these rights and that is why i believe we must support this report, because it is a decisive step in establishing minimum standards and in the fight against illegal work and the exploitation of migrant workers.
madam president, this draft directive, which is of paramount importance in the fight against illegal immigration, was essential for the establishment of a common immigration policy. we all know that illegal employment is the main attraction of the thousands of men and women who cross our borders every day, hoping to find decent work and feed their families. in reality, they often face employers who use and abuse their fragile situation and lack of awareness of their rights to exploit them and use them as cheap labour. it's called modern slavery. we must not hide the fact that this phenomenon also affects persons, european citizens or nationals of third countries, who are legally resident but do not fall within the scope of this directive, which is precisely part of the fight against illegal immigration. this is not to point the finger at the men and women who are often well-meaning but who fall victim to dishonest networks or employers. the purpose of this text must be precisely madam president, i would first of all like to congratulate our colleague, mr claudio fava, on his excellent work, which will lead to the adoption of a directive providing for sanctions against employers of illegal workers. however, i would like to draw your attention to the complexity of the present situation, because we have to develop legislation that is commensurate with this complexity. throughout the european union, contractors are increasingly using cascade subcontractors from member countries, without knowing whether the employees employed are in legal status. an amendment had been proposed to check the legality of the situation of their employees. why wasn't he integrated? on the other hand, it is provided that the main contractor is responsible for the payment of wages, but only if he knew that the subcontractors employed illegal nationals. but you will not find any employer who will, of course, willingly admit his guilt. in the end, the best directive will only be effective if the means of control are actually put in place. we could take these checks a step further by strengthening the number and role of labour inspectors in each european country. it is essential to devise an even more rigorous legal framework as soon as possible so that the contractors are held fully responsible in the event of subcontractors' failure. we must not, therefore, ignore the known practices of certain economic sectors which are complicit in organized illegal immigration.
in writing. this report has several merits. the first is educational: it sets out the alarming trend of the increase in illegal immigration in europe: an immigration estimated by the commission's own figures at between 4.5 million and 8 million, and it identifies the sectors of the economy in which illegal work is most concentrated: construction, agriculture, cleaning, the hotel and catering industry. the second merit is that of intensifying the fight against undeclared work, in particular by the possibility of financial and criminal sanctions against employers of illegal workers. unfortunately, there are many limitations to this relationship. there is no mention of what measures should be taken to stop these intermittent flows of illegal immigration. the reintroduction of internal border controls is not even contemplated. in addition, in times of social and economic crisis and of a sharp rise in unemployment, the first necessity for the countries of the union is to protect their jobs. this requires the establishment of national and european policies of social protectionism. we must reserve jobs for french people in france and for europeans in europe. it is the application of the principles of national and european preference and protection as essential conditions for the economic and social recovery of the countries of the european union.
in writing. everyone is aware that the energy issue is a major issue for the member states. energy savings, improvements in energy efficiency, research and the commercialisation of renewable energy or new technologies in transport, diversification of suppliers - all these are known ways of reducing dependence. and we do not dispute the need for some cooperation, or even the organization, on an intergovernmental basis, of solidarity between states. but in reality it seems that the development of an energy strategy or security of supply is much less important in the report than the establishment of a single energy policy or a single gas and electricity network under the auspices of a single european regulator for each sector. however, the choices, needs, opportunities and capacities of states remain extremely different. this sensitive issue is indeed strategic and as such should be the sole responsibility of the sovereign will of the states and the respect of their interests. but the aim is once again to increase the powers of the brussels bureaucracy. from skyrocketing electricity prices to regular power outages, we know what to expect when it comes to electricity efficiency. that is why we voted against this report.
in writing. the report again proposes the nuclear option, since this energy is not competitive and uranium is obtained under dangerous conditions, with ethnic discrimination and with unacceptable health impacts. coal, in the face of the problem of global warming, should not be considered a 'transitional component'. i believe that the 'diversification of eu energy resources' is linked to the exploitation of fossil resources in the caspian sea. oil and gas fields in the kashagan region put pressure on the population and its environmental resources: the extraction of sulphur-laden oil puts the health of the population and biodiversity at risk. diversification of energy supply involves pipelines of gas and oil to bring resources to the eu. the tbc or nabucco projects are a threat to the political stability of our neighbours and force us not to compromise it by our energy needs. the people of the south caucasus must derive economic and social benefits from the supply of energy from their territories. in africa, the production of solar energy for our needs must be properly remunerated. why not say in the report that renewable energy and energy saving are the solution for the future? as things stand, i am voting against this report.
in writing. from ms záborská's explanatory memorandum we learn that the aim of her report is the fair social and economic recognition of certain activities which cannot be defined as 'formal market employment'. in short, the main focus is on child rearing, but also, in our ageing societies, on the care of dependent persons. this was worth mentioning, because it is not obvious at first sight, not in the title of the report, which speaks of discrimination, or even at first reading of a text written in a sometimes strange style. in short, the text rightly speaks of recognition by society, of the inclusion in national accounts of all this wealth created, although invisible, of freedom of choice, and even mentions the granting of specific rights in the field of social security and retirement to those who would choose to devote themselves to their family rather than to a career. it is a pity, however, that mrs záborská does not go to the end of her logic by forgetting the only measure which is really capable of allowing both a real freedom of choice and a revival of birth by removing the financial constraint: the parental wage, which the national front has been proposing for years.
in writing. child sexual abuse and child pornography are particularly heinous crimes which, in the age of the internet and sex tourism, deserve stronger legislation, increased cooperation between police and judicial services and better support for victims. the report by mrs angelilli deserves our support. but i would like to remind you that apart from technological developments that increase the opportunities for perverts to fulfill their vice, we must also look to moral decay and the degradation of values as one of the reasons for the rise of this type of crime. only thirty years ago, in the name of a supposed liberalization of morals, unfettered enjoyment for all and a pseudo-personal fulfillment of the individual from an early age, a certain political movement promoted the sexual activities of children, including in the columns of the french newspaper le monde, the organ of the left of the salons. if this vile speech is, let us hope, now rejected, its authors continue to perpetrate it and their political movement continues to give lessons without ever having made a mea culpa. one last comment: why is the only right that is not recognized for children in most of our states is their right to be born?

mr president, in our cultures where the rule of law and human rights have been established, it is good to defend the rights of the minority individual, but it is quickly dangerous to legislate on the rights of non-national minorities as communities. for non-national minorities, and i shall confine my discussion to this, the community approach must be rejected because it will inevitably destroy the cohesion of many european nations. in the rule of law, the regulation of the will to live together must remain a matter for national competence. in this case, the majority cannot be the opponent of the minority, unless they have a definite doubt about democracy. poverty or threats have forced some to flee their homeland and seek refuge. the right to asylum is a kind of vote with the feet. fortunately, it has become a fundamental right. but, as with any right, the counterpart is duty. in this case, it is the obligation to conform to the rules, language, and customs of the host country. the right to asylum is a precious right because it is an inherent right of the human person. even if one belongs to a minority, it does not legitimize the birth of a community law. the ultimate allegiance must always be to the country in which one is settled. it is an illusion to believe that the juxtaposition of communities of passage, of separate memories, makes a country. in time, it becomes a field of indifference or battle. the host country, you either love it or you leave it. this is the responsibility that comes with freedom to come and go.

in writing. the florenz report sets out a very detailed list of actions to be taken to combat climate change and develop accompanying policies. it is, however, fraught with structural weaknesses which point to the necessary and desirable reorientation of the european union. the big shortages are financial. if the creation of a carbon tax is envisaged, its study and implementation, like that of a systematic carbon balance sheet by product, are not included in the 2009-2014 action programme! but it is a vital element. no budgetary amount is mentioned for specific and targeted actions and projects, whether for public infrastructure or innovative industrial policies, regional development, aid to local authorities or research/development. in industrial matters, the reference to 'legislative instruments' cannot be sufficient. similarly, the creation of a european climate fund is subject to the imperative 'to leave it to the market to determine which technologies should be used...'. it will therefore not have a long-term vision or the general interest ... it is absurd. it is therefore essential that the eu addresses very quickly the issue of a carbon tax, public aid to support a green new deal, and the eu budget for climate change prevention.
in writing. i voted in favour of the fava report on the draft directive which provides for sanctions against employers of illegal immigrants. according to commission figures, between 4.5 and 8 million third-country nationals live clandestinely in the european union and are therefore the prime targets of unscrupulous employers who make their living from clandestine work. it is essential for us to put more emphasis on these practices which are unworthy of a europe where respect for fundamental rights must apply to all. the time has come to finally emphasize the responsibility of those who take advantage of this particularly vulnerable population. we must stop criminalizing these exploited people by stigmatizing illegal immigrants. the measures we are advocating here are not only to punish abusive bosses but also to defend a number of social rights such as the right to be represented by a trade union. however, we must not claim victory too soon, because the threat of sanctions is not enough, we must also have the legal instruments of control that go with it. only then will we be able to put in place an effective common immigration policy.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by a very large majority of the draft directive, which is of paramount importance in the fight against illegal immigration and is essential for the establishment of a comprehensive common immigration policy. the illegal employment is the main attraction of the thousands of men and women who cross our borders every day hoping to find decent work there to feed their families. in reality, they are simply becoming slaves to certain employers who use and abuse their fragile situation and lack of knowledge of their rights to exploit them and use them as cheap labour. this directive sends a double message: one to fraudulent employers, who will no longer be able to abuse the situation with impunity, and the other to illegal immigrants, who will be deterred by stricter conditions for access to legal employment. the compromise reached with the council is satisfactory and we can only hope that the member states will implement this directive swiftly to put an end to the vulnerability of thousands of people in europe.

member of the commission. − mr president, the european commission wishes to express its sadness at the number of lives claimed by storm klaus and sends its condolences to the french, italian and spanish families that have lost loved ones. this is indeed a human tragedy, which has had a devastating impact on people’s lives, homes and businesses. it is also an ecological disaster. while this storm was extremely powerful, it only affected a narrow band of territory, and national resources have been able to cope with the immediate disaster response. for this reason, the community civil protect mechanism was not activated. however, the commission’s monitoring and information centre has been in close contact with the concerned member states from the first moments when the storm was forecast. other member states were aware of the situation and were getting prepared to provide support to the affected regions. for example, the czech republic spontaneously offered its assistance. the commission is now cooperating with the authorities of the member states affected in order to identify options for eu support. possibilities may include through the eu solidarity fund or a reprogramming of the structural and rural development funds. storm klaus is an unpleasant reminder that natural disasters are a growing threat for all eu member states. devastating floods hit central europe in 2000 and 2002, the uk in 2007, and romania and eu neighbours last year. the 2003 heatwave claimed tens of thousands of lives. in 2003 and 2007 forest fires ravaged portugal and greece. these events give us an idea of how climate change is likely to affect the eu’s future because, as the climate changes, we can expect more extreme weather events. the member states and the community need to combine their strengths to prevent disasters, to limit their impacts and to improve the union’s disaster response capacity. the commission will shortly adopt a communication on ‘a community approach on the prevention of natural and man-made disasters’. we look forward to receiving feedback from the parliament on the ideas that are set out. the commission would also stress the importance of moving forward on the revision of the solidarity fund regulation. the proposal helps to accelerate the rate of response by allowing for advance payments, and it contains simpler criteria for an activation of the fund in less time. while the parliament largely supported the commission proposal, there has been no progress in the council. these initiatives are contributing to shape a genuine european disaster management policy, and the commission hopes that the european parliament will continue to support its efforts to reinforce the eu’s capacity to deal with natural and man-made disasters.

rapporteur. − mr president, 70 years ago mr chamberlain came back from munich waving a piece of paper and saying ‘peace for our time’. well, we know how wrong he was, and we also know that wishful thinking is a deadly substitute for realism. today, on this issue, we have to be brutally honest. the eu has been incredibly successful in peace-making. the events of the second world war gave birth to the eu. i am very happy that mr solana is here today because finally we have this phone number for the eu. mr solana has this number, which mr kissinger asked for years ago. but what kinds of means are we – member states and politicians – giving to mr solana? member of the commission. − mr president, it is a pleasure to be here today to talk about children and also about the report you will adopt shortly. let me talk for a few minutes about how we got to where we are today and what will come in the future and about child participation, which is most likely our biggest challenge regarding children. today is an important step in a long process that started several years ago internally in the commission. we recognise that the eu needs a strategy on children. we need a strategy on how we, the european union, will implement the commitments. we and the rest of the world have signed up to the un convention on the rights of the child. the first step was the commission communication ‘towards an eu strategy on the rights of the child’ in 2006. this was followed in 2008 by the communication package on children in external actions, which outlined a comprehensive approach to children by the eu using all available instruments in external cooperation. let me digress for a moment, since i am convinced that some of you will be asking the question: what about the eu strategy on the rights of the child, which was announced in the above-mentioned communication? i can confirm that the commission is working on such a strategy, which will be presented under the next commission. during the slovenian presidency in may 2008, the council adopted conclusions on the promotion and protection of the rights of the child in the european union’s external action – the development of humanitarian dimensions. the committee on development then started drafting a report and we are now at the end of this process and tomorrow you will be voting on this excellent report. in addition, the eu’s policy on children is based on the two eu guidelines – the guidelines on children in armed conflicts and the guidelines on the rights of the child – both being implemented in a number of selected priority and pilot countries. the commission welcomes the report – which is an excellent complement to our communication – the council conclusions and the guidelines. we will surely use it in our work on children. let me focus my last comments on what is probably our biggest challenge today: child participation. how do we ensure that we involve children in decisions that concern them? how do we ensure that children have access to pertinent information? how do we ensure equal access for children to express their views? we have to recognise that, amongst everything that we all agreed to in the convention on the rights of the child, this might be the major challenge. we have to admit that we are still far from achieving anything significant in the area of child participation. in the commission we are starting to reflect on how to design and implement proper child participation that is not just tokenism. it should be relevant, meaningful and informed child participation. we have also ensured relevant funding for child participation under the thematic programme ‘investing in people’. why is this difficult for us adults? essentially, because it questions what is fundamental to us: the way we behave. what will the commission do in its external action to promote this participation? the commission will make the tools available for our delegations to consult children, but these tools will be used not only by our delegations but also by partner countries. we are also developing a tool kit, together with unicef, that should not only address the child participation but also overall child protection, legal reform, child budgeting. in addition to the tool kit, we are also recasting and strengthening our collaboration with unicef in general in order to be able to improve our support to partner countries in their efforts to ensure that children have a voice at country level. we also cooperate closely with various ngos to learn from them about possible formats, often involving children and having meaningful child participation. let me honest: it is not going to happen tomorrow. this is just the start of a long process. let me just make one comment on the report. the report underlines how the commission should pay attention to child participation, but, colleagues, you will also have to do so, and i can assure you that the commission will be happy to work with you on advancing this. we should build on the collective force of the two institutions to advance this important issue. let me once again express the commission’s appreciation of the report and underline that we will do our utmost to carry out these recommendations. we are counting on the continued support of parliament in this area. in answer to ms kinnock’s question, i am happy to confirm that the position of the commission has not changed. the idea of using 2009 for consultations was launched in the commission itself and we are working to put in place the conditions for a process of consultation with children that avails itself of all existing tools. let me also underline that the commission is keen to ensure a process of consultation that fully respects the rights of the child. finally, let me thank you, the agenda calls for the brief presentation of the report by jean louis cottigny, on behalf of the committee on employment and social affairs, on the application of directive 2002/14/ec establishing a general framework for the information and consultation of workers in the european community (2008/2246 (ini)) (a6-0023/2009).
the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should first like to thank the various fictitious rapporteurs for their open-minded work during our collaboration on this text in the committee on employment. member states should improve the implementation of the directive on information and consultation of workers, in particular in the current context of the financial crisis and its consequences in terms of restructuring, mergers and relocations of undertakings. this is the message that the committee on employment has wished to convey in this own-initiative report. there are 23 million enterprises in the european union with fewer than 250 employees. they represent 99% of enterprises and employ over 100 million people. the right of workers to information and consultation is an essential component of the social market economy. the transposition of directive 2002/14/ec has been considerably delayed in some member states. in this own-initiative report we point out that the impact of this directive is evident in countries where no general system of information and consultation of workers existed. i call for better transposition of the directive in the member states. we urge the commission to take measures as soon as possible to ensure that the directive is properly transposed by the member states and to initiate infringement proceedings against those who have not transposed it or have not transposed it correctly. the report also points out that in their transposition measures some member states have not taken account of certain young workers, women working part-time or workers employed for a short period under fixed-term contracts. we call on the member states to define precisely the term 'information' by allowing workers' representatives to examine the data provided and not to wait for the information procedure to be completed if the decisions of the undertakings have direct consequences for the workers. member states that do not have effective, proportionate and dissuasive sanctions are invited to introduce them. finally, in order to achieve better coordination of the various legislative instruments, we also invite the commission to examine the coordination requirements of the six directives and the regulation on information for workers, with a view to making any changes to eliminate overlaps and contradictions. because this kind of advance in workers' rights is more than beneficial, the union has a duty to ensure that the states transpose the obligations of the directive correctly and completely. it is essential that all european workers know that europe supports them in their involvement in the life of their company, in their daily lives as workers, and above all in the present times.

the agenda calls for the brief presentation of the report by patrizia toia, on behalf of the committee on employment and social affairs, on the social economy (2008/2250 (ini)) (a6-0015/2009).
member of the commission. − mr president, the commission welcomes parliament’s initiative to formulate an own-initiative opinion on the social economy. especially in the context of the present financial and economic crisis, this important sector deserves to be promoted more. social economy enterprises have a unique way of doing business since they combine economic performance mutually between members, and often also the achievement of social and societal objectives, as a business purpose. thus, they are well placed to contribute to community policies and objectives, particularly in the field of employment, social cohesion, regional and rural development, environmental protection, consumer protection and social security. social economy enterprises are an integral part of the commission’s enterprise policy. since in the majority they are micro-, small- or medium-sized enterprises, they already benefit from the small business act and all actions targeting small enterprises. with regard to the social economy, our objective is to create a legal and administrative environment, at european level and in every member state, in which social economy enterprises of whatever form and size can thrive and meet the challenges posed by globalisation and the economic downturn. more specifically, the commission’s policy aims to guarantee that social economy enterprises can grow and prosper alongside other forms of company. to this end, the commission pays particular attention to ensuring that all other community policies in areas such as competition, accounting, company law, public procurement, health, social affairs, agriculture, fisheries, banking, insurance, public and private partnerships and regional development, do take into account the specific needs, particular goals, efforts and working style of this kind of enterprise. to conclude, the commission services are currently working on a document which will take stock of the progress made since 2004 on the promotion of cooperatives. it will also assess the situation of other social economy enterprises and propose new actions if necessary.

the agenda calls for the brief presentation of the report by mrs tzampazi, on behalf of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, on mental health (2008/2209 (ini)) (a6-0034/2009).
member of the commission. − mr president, i congratulate the european parliament and its rapporteur, ms tzampazi, on this own-initiative report on mental health. the report quite rightly underlines the great impact mental health has on general well-being, on education, on learning, and on social cohesion in the european union. the fact that parliament is adopting this report only two years after a resolution responding to the commission’s green paper on mental health signals the urgent need for more action in this field. in my view there is some reason for optimism. there is more awareness of the importance of mental health and well-being across all sectors, compared to a few years ago. this was evident from the great support for the commission’s high-level conference ‘together for mental health and well-being’ and the european pact for mental health and well-being, both of which were mentioned by the rapporteur. further positive developments include the fact that many member states have revised their mental health strategies or are setting up action plans, for example in finland and hungary. socio-economic learning has been included in school curricula. in the united kingdom, life issues are now a subject in their own right in many schools. employers are increasingly aware of the links between well-being and productivity. csr europe has even created a toolkit for well-being in the workplace. however, let us be clear, there can certainly be no reason for complacency, and much more remains to be done. there could be new risks for mental health as a result of the current financial and economic crisis. member states could be tempted to reduce budgets for mental health or to reduce their efforts to build up modern mental health systems with community-based services instead of outdated asylums. the economic downturn worsens the future prospects of young people, especially school leavers. job insecurity in the workplace, and its ensuing concerns over the stability of incomes and rising levels of unemployment, create new major threats for mental health. over the next two years the commission will organise a series of thematic conferences on the five priorities of the mental health pact. these will be joint events with council presidencies and member states. a first international conference on stigma and psychiatric care will be organised by the czech presidency on 29 may this year. the first thematic conference on mental health in youth and education will take place in stockholm on 29-30 september, in cooperation with the swedish presidency. the second thematic conference on prevention of depression and suicide will be organised with hungary in december. in the first semester of 2010, the spanish presidency will host a thematic conference on the mental health of older people. furthermore, we are in contact with member states regarding two further conferences on mental health in workplace settings and on combating stigma and social exclusion. parliament’s report includes many concrete suggestions, which constitute a valuable contribution to future debates in these conferences. the report not only highlights the relevance of mental health in the european union, but also demonstrates that there are many opportunities to act in the area of mental health at european union level. one of the suggestions in the report is to set up a structure to oversee the implementation of the european pact for mental health and well-being. i agree that there would be significant added value in periodically reviewing progress against the objectives of the pact. we will seriously consider how we can best put such an idea into practice. once again, i would like to thank parliament and its rapporteur for this very supportive report and its very important recommendations.
the point is closed. the vote will take place on thursday 19 february 2009. written declarations (article 142) the following documents shall be submitted to the court of justice:

member of the commission. − mr president, i welcome the opportunity to address this part-session of the european parliament covering, inter alia, the subject of the commission’s assessment of the national energy efficiency action plans (neeaps), which was presented in the second strategic energy review package in november 2008 and the earlier commission communication of january 2008. a more detailed technical synthesis of the commission’s assessment of the neeaps will be presented in the commission’s neeap document this spring. i would, therefore, like to take this opportunity to thank the rapporteur, mr gyürk, on his work, as well as the committee on industry, research and energy (itre) for its valuable discussions and comments. in the past few years, the commission has stated very clearly that energy efficiency is the first priority of the european union energy policy and a very important cornerstone to meeting the 2020 by 2020 targets, and national energy efficiency action plans play a central role in this respect. the directive on energy end-use efficiency and energy services sets an obligation, as you know, for the member states to present these, and to show how in practice they are going to achieve their national targets for energy efficiency. the original deadline for their submission by the member states was 30 june 2007 but, as you know, many member states unfortunately were late. the last neeaps arrived at the commission in june 2008. at this stage, the commission has completed all the individual assessments and sent letters with the results of those assessments to all the member states. as a follow-up, a number of bilateral meetings took place, and a number of member states declared they would themselves like to improve their neeaps in the coming few months. as has been noted by the members of the itre committee, the first national energy efficiency action plans have proved to be a really useful exercise. indeed, many member states have, for the first time, prepared comprehensive plans of action on energy savings. many of them confirmed that they found the cross-sectoral effort needed to prepare them very useful. under the energy services directive, neeaps have only a limited role. however, the commission, in its communication of november 2008, and in other recent statements has always encouraged member states to broaden their role. the commission will prepare a new european union energy savings action plan that will strengthen and better focus european union actions, helping eu member states and eu businesses and eu citizens to save energy in a cost-effective way. in your report you urged the commission to propose a binding target for energy savings. the current energy savings objective of 20% of primary energy saving in 2020 today represents a non-binding target, as you know. however, the commission believes that, with the climate and energy package, as well as the proposals in the second strategic energy review, we can reach 20%. mr gyürk’s report also rightly indicated that financial support must be increased. financial issues relating to energy savings were recognised by the commission in the european economic recovery plan of 26 november 2008, and in other coordinated efforts which aim to help create jobs, which are often in small- and medium-sized companies, since investments in energy efficiency, and especially in buildings, are mostly related to small-scale renovation projects. in conclusion, i would like to recall that during the mandate of this commission, eu leaders have given a real commitment to promoting energy efficiency. boosting investment in energy efficiency and related new technologies offers an essential contribution to sustainable development and also to security of supply. energy efficiency has a wider impact, far beyond energy policy. it has a positive effect on the european union economy in general: increasing efficiency helps create new jobs, stimulates economic growth and improves competitiveness. as you rightly mentioned, that is exactly what we should be doing in these difficult and challenging times.
the point is closed. the vote will take place on thursday 19 february 2009. written declarations (article 142) the following documents shall be submitted to the court of justice:

for the gue/ngl group mr president, commissioner, the draft statute for the european private company is presented by the commission as part of the small business act for europe. the initial idea was to reserve a certain share of public contracts for small firms, as is the case in the united states. such noble intentions were to be applauded. unfortunately, when we arrive at the spe, it is a completely different matter. first, the size of the firms concerned. the small enterprise has been replaced by the already much more vague concept of small and mediumsized enterprises, and finally - i quote the explanatory memorandum to the draft regulation adopted by the commission - a 'status which can also benefit larger companies and groups'. this completely changes the philosophy of the approach, and therefore, what will happen to the fake smes? in reality, subsidiaries of multinational companies have long been demanding a single status which is less restrictive than the status they now enjoy for the companies they control in various european countries. let us now consider the nature of the advantages offered to companies benefiting from spe status. it is no longer a question of facilitating access to public procurement, but - i quote again the explanatory statement of the commission's text - of improving the framework conditions for businesses in the single market. to this end, all private european companies could have their headquarters in one country and their actual activities in another. they could also move their headquarters to a member state of their choice. how can we not see these provisions as a means of enabling the companies concerned to set up, without any other constraints, the most business-friendly letterbox companies under the heavens? does the commission not state that the applicable law is that of the member state of the registered office of the spe in respect of limited liability companies? as the european trade union confederation rightly points out, there is a great risk that companies will use the spe's statutes to evade the most protective legislation for workers. it is easy to understand why the commission did not consult the trade union organisations before adopting its proposal, and instead merely consulted them online. in summary, it is clear from the draft regulation that the emphasis on small businesses is above all a matter of political dress to make a new version of the infamous principle of the country of origin presentable. it's a bolkestein with a new look. that is why my group proposes that parliament send a clear signal to the commission and the council by rejecting this draft statute for a european private company.
