in writing. consumers are increasingly demanding on the quality, origin and safety of agricultural products. the eu has succeeded in establishing a quality labelling system that guarantees the authenticity of products that are characteristic of a territory or of traditional manufacture. the eu and its member states therefore have a duty to promote these high-quality products and to better protect them at international level. this means guaranteeing fair competition between european products and those from third countries, in particular by protecting european farmers against any product that usurps a name. products at risk of misappropriation should thus be granted international protection in the wto and any application for registration of a protected indication from third countries should be subject to more stringent controls. in order to better inform the consumer, it is important that the country of origin of the primary products and, in the case of processed products, the origin of the main ingredients and the place of last processing be indicated on the label. at the same time, the eu must uphold the principle of 'conditional market access' by recommending that the wto adopt stricter protection standards for quality products so that imported products are subject to the same safety and quality requirements as european products.
vice-president of the commission. - madam president, i should first like to thank mr medina ortega for raising a number of very important questions. it is true that this regulation should be better known to the judges and practitioners in each country. it should be noted that the direct execution of an investigation order under article 17 of the regulation has simplified and accelerated the taking of evidence without posing any particular problem. the central bodies provided for in that regulation have an important role to play in monitoring the courts that are required to deal with applications submitted under this regulation and in resolving problems encountered by them. the assistance provided by central bodies can be essential for small courts facing a problem of obtaining evidence in a cross-border context for the first time. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the information provided by the member states is not misused. the european judicial network in civil and commercial matters - you mentioned it - normally has the task of facilitating this judicial cooperation in europe as well. since its entry into force, the implementation of the gtr has been the focus of the network's work on several occasions. a practical guide on the application of the regulation was produced in 2006 and distributed to all european courts in 2007. the european judicial network in civil and commercial matters can, through its contact points, and you are right, mr medina ortega, to be more involved in the execution of requests for evidence that are more respectful of the time limits laid down in the regulation. i did. i'm trying to move on and see some perspective. it is true that the regulation lays down precise criteria as to the form and content of the application. the application must be made in a specific form and contain certain information: the name, address of the parties to the proceedings, the nature and subject matter of the case, a description of the evidence to be provided. the rules of procedure also state that the application must be submitted in one of the official languages of the member state of the court seised, or in any other language which the member state seised has indicated it will accept, but as you have just pointed out, this is not the least of the linguistic problems. a request for evidence should normally be executed promptly. if it is not possible to comply with the request within 90 days of receipt by the requested court, the requested court shall inform the requesting court accordingly, stating the reasons. in fact, the possibility of refusing to comply with the request for the taking of evidence is limited to exceptional situations, strictly limited situations. that was the rule. a study on its application was carried out in march 2007 and it was on the basis of the results of this study that the commission adopted a report in december 2007. the report was drawn up in accordance with article 23 of the regulation. what's he saying? the application of the regulation has rather improved, been simplified and has nevertheless accelerated cooperation between courts on the taking of evidence in civil and commercial matters. thus, it has already achieved two main objectives: to simplify cooperation between member states and to speed up the collection of evidence. simplification has been achieved, in particular, by the introduction of direct transmission from court to court although sometimes requests go back to the central bodies and by the introduction of standard forms. progress has also been made in speeding up the processing of requests for evidence. most of them are being carried out more quickly than before the regulation came into force - fortunately - within the 90 days provided for in the regulation. mr medina ortega, i would therefore say that we do not see the need to amend the rules of procedure. but its functioning must be improved. in its action plan adopted in november 2008, the council entrusted the commission with the implementation of the european e-justice portal. the completion of the portal, including the first phase of the portal, which will be operational this year, is obviously a top priority for us and for me. as regards the use of videoconferencing, we will also make it a priority. the european judicial network in civil and commercial matters is currently preparing a practical guide on the legal aspects of the use of videoconferencing in the taking of evidence. of course, this practical guide will be sent to the european judges and will be completed by the end of this year. it will be written in the portal, which, as i told you, will be published before the end of the year. the court of justice has not yet been equipped with videoconferencing equipment. we hope to take advantage of the new financing arrangements when the financial perspective for 2010-13 is revised. there are already funding opportunities for crossborder projects in the civil justice programme, where the use of videoconferencing is highlighted as a priority. i would say to you, mr medina ortega, that i agree with you on a major point, judges. i believe that this will be one of the guidelines of the next stockholm programme. in any case, thank you for this report, which is very helpful and informative.

in writing. what is rare deserves to be highlighted. this own-initiative report on the future of the management of the union's external borders is reasonable and realistic in that it proposes, as a first step in thinking about the management of the union's borders, a critical and in-depth analysis of the functioning and effectiveness of the existing systems and their respective interactions. i do not want to be gullible, but i am optimistic that this debate will take place. to illustrate, and to help you understand the mindset of the writers of this text, here are two passages from it. the first acknowledges that "the balance to be struck between ensuring the free movement of an increasing number of people across borders and ensuring greater security for european citizens is a complex exercise". indeed, and another passage says: 'measures to strengthen border security must go hand in hand with measures to facilitate passenger flows and promote mobility in an increasingly globalised world'. such a level of schizophrenia is beyond us.
in writing. as the socialist shadow on this issue, i have from the outset expressed serious reservations about the usefulness and efficiency of the entry-exit system mentioned in the european commission's communication. the establishment of such a system, directly inspired by the us-visit system, would require enormous investments with very uncertain results in both the fight against illegal immigration and the fight against crime. this is what the transatlantic experiment shows. in addition, the proposed measures, which rely on the mass collection of personal data, in my view pose risks to the protection of privacy, an opinion shared by the european data protection supervisor. the adoption of a number of my amendments, which aimed to highlight the doubts about the necessity and proportionality of the system and to criticise the culture of mistrust which is increasingly permeating decisions on the management of the external borders, led me to support the report in plenary. at a time when the world economy is in crisis, there are probably other priorities for the european budget.
in writing. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report by giusto catania, member of the european parliament for the unitary left, on the future of the common european asylum system. the text of this report deals with the situation of asylum seekers whose fate is a lottery depending on the country they arrive in, and whose conditions of detention are sometimes on the verge of being unbearable. this is a situation which particularly affects the border countries but which requires consideration at european level. the fundamental rights of asylum seekers are at stake. the ability of some countries to cope with these migratory pressures, too. this is a shared responsibility. the report has the merit of providing a clear assessment of the situation and of clarifying the challenges facing the european union in this debate. i am therefore voting along with the french socialists to denounce a situation which is no longer acceptable and which europe, as a democratic institution and protector of human rights, must remedy.
in writing. the basic idea of the catania report is that an applicant for international protection must be in good faith, whereas everyone knows that asylum is often just a pretext used by economic immigration applicants to avoid being turned away. the member states, on the other hand, are supposedly necessarily deaf to their plight, repressive and too slow in their decisions. no one has pointed out that the abuse of illegitimate procedures is detrimental to the speed with which genuine asylum applications are examined. the report's proposals are probably based on these premises, such as taking account of the wishes of the applicant for the country responsible for examining his application, the designation of this country by a european administration, the alignment of the rights of applicants with those of long-term residents, their free movement within the territory of the european union, etc. we welcome the necessary cooperation with european countries whose geographical situation puts them at the forefront of the influx of migrants and who are having difficulty coping with it. but in no case should this lead to a european policy which would impose on the states, according to the good will of the asylum seekers and a supranational administration, those whom they would be obliged to welcome on their territory.
in writing. the desire to create a common european asylum system actually has only one objective: to give the member states of the european union the legal possibility to receive as many immigration applicants as possible more easily and without constraints (unnecessary judgments that are contrary to human rights). the european territory is thus reaffirmed as a territory of welcome for all migrant populations, and full respect for the principle of non-refoulement and the obligation to provide assistance enshrined in the united nations convention on the law of the sea are emphatically recalled. therefore, and this is understandable for these pro-immigrationists, the mere fact that each member state retains its sovereignty and its own functioning in terms of asylum law inevitably allows for disparities in the acceptance of asylum applications and therefore constitutes obstacles to a widespread reception of asylum seekers. with nearly 26 million people displaced within their own countries and more than 12 million refugees worldwide, the need is not to find more reception solutions, which will always be insufficient in the face of growing and exponential demand, but on the contrary to enable and encourage all these populations to stay in their countries, to find employment and to start their families there.
in writing. the report by the communist catania favours the implementation of a european immigration policy. under the guise of defending human rights, he wants to make europe an open community, ready to welcome all the misery in the world. the commission is proposing to extend the scope of the directive on the status of third-country nationals who are long-term residents to refugees. mr catania pretends to forget that most of the illegal immigrants arriving in europe - 75,000 in 2008 just for the mediterranean front - are not political refugees but economic refugees fleeing the misery in their own countries. this misuse of the right of asylum, contrary to the geneva convention, is never mentioned in the report, and for good reason. the "white man" should be made to feel guilty by being reminded that he was a terrible colonialist and that he must now pay in every sense of the word. legends have a hard time with life. mr catania, in his desire to make asylum a normal part of immigration, is opening the way to many abuses and making scapegoats of illegal immigrants.

for. this is very important, because it means that ships cannot call at places where they are certain to escape inspection. secondly, we have obtained very strict procedures for the implementation of between inspections of these vessels shall not exceed six months. but the most satisfactory part of our negotiations with the council is that repeated misconduct will be punished. inspections in our ports may result in temporary measures of denial of access and prohibitions of navigation in our waters. this could lead to a permanent ban, i.e. a definitive ban on entering european ports and anchorages. the waste vessels are the ones that are affected by this measure. to do this, there will be a tolerance limit, a threshold of irresponsibility that must not be crossed, because ships that are permanently banned from our ports or anchorages will be designated as floating garbage, which should have a deterrent effect. we have obtained the council's agreement on this in conciliation. the the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, we are now at the end of a legislative marathon which was mentioned here as having lasted ten years and which is being misnamed, as we were told this morning in a debate on 'erika iii'. first of all, because after the erika, there was the prestige; after the prestige, there was the tricolor; the tricolor was followed by many other maritime accidents in european waters and beyond. and above all, because, as dirk sterckx has reminded us, it is a cold legislation, the first, that is to say, a legislation free of the passions, excesses and controversies that take place after disasters such as the prestige or the erika. i think it is a credit to jacques barrot and the commission that they have proposed it, but it was also a formidable difficulty. member states are not very inclined to legislate in areas like these when nothing serious is going on. in fact, they sometimes legislate when there are too many accidents. in any case, it is indeed very important legislation, since it contains seven texts. what is his goal? to make the european maritime area - rather than the member states' - one of the safest in the world. and it's quite legitimate because it's also one of the busiest in the world and it's also, geographically, one of the most complicated in the world. we have many straits: the bosphorus, gibraltar, the calais strait - where 800 merchant ships cross every day - which are among the largest ports on the planet. we have therefore had to make this considerable effort, not unfortunately to ensure that there will be no more accidents, because life is always random, but to ensure that, on the one hand, accidents are prevented as far as possible and, on the other hand, that the causes of accidents are punished. the architecture of this package is simple: it is that of the virtuous circle, where every element of the transport chain - from the port state to the insurer, through the shipowner, the classification society and the flag state - is responsible for its actions and, somewhere, presses, that is, the bet, to clean up the conditions of transport and moralize them, and make sure to check that we have a virtuous carrier who complies with the standards. in fact, when we think about it, our model today, in its main principles and architecture, might be worth inspiring what we are trying to do in the financial field. the financial rating agencies have been as deficient as the maritime rating agencies. some states have what are called tax havens. some operators are undesirable and are subject to blacklists or bans in the maritime sector. it is therefore a very exemplary piece of legislation, which is also part of the international imo framework. i would also like to say that on the political level this is a remarkable community achievement, since the link between the commission and parliament has led to a very complicated text and legislation, to which there was very strong reluctance in the member states. i would like to thank antonio tajani and the commission. i would also like to thank the french presidency, because i think dominique bussereau realised that this could be something very important during the french presidency; and i would like to thank all my colleagues, because everyone here knows that we used subterfuge and deception to get this done. we have succeeded in imposing this maritime package only because we were united and we were so united that some colleagues have inherited, if i may say so, illegal passengers, such as my text or mr jardim fernandes' text, which the council did not want. that, ladies and gentlemen, is the reason for this success. i would have liked to elaborate on my report, but i think i have a final opportunity to speak, and this will be the occasion to do so. in writing. eight pieces of legislation forming part of a maritime package have just been adopted by the european parliament. we welcome this, because this package covers not only compensation for passengers but also inspections, port state control, transport accident investigations and the choice of the authority deciding where to shelter ships in distress. the ball is now in the court of the member states, because it is not enough to legislate, it is also necessary to transpose into their national legislation. the first test will be the control of flags of complacency of european countries. these flags are used to circumvent the union, tax, recruitment, security or environmental regulations of the country of real ownership. cyprus and malta are still in the top five lists of lost ships. it is regrettable that despite the efforts made since the prestige and erika oil tankers sank, the situation has not improved. substandard ships, under flag of convenience, are driving down transportation prices. the so-called rich countries, in response, are building their own tent (bis) in order to combat the loss of freight. in fact, to really eliminate these floating wrecks, the european union must tackle ultraliberalism.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report by the czech mep jaromír kohlíček, on the investigation of accidents in the shipping sector. the text stresses the need for clear and binding guidelines at european level to ensure effective monitoring of accidents at sea. it responds to the concerns following the sinking of the oil tanker erika off the french coast. it is to prevent mismanagement like this from happening again that the european union has decided to impose a strict framework, which deals with all the technical aspects and all the procedures to be followed in the event of an accident: methodology of investigations, european database on maritime accidents, safety instructions, etc. i share the view that it is essential to make the european maritime area one of the most exemplary and safe in the world. this is the aim of the maritime package, also known as 'erika iii', of which this report forms part. this is a real leap forward for the maritime sector, and also for the environment, which is often a collateral victim of poor maritime behaviour.
in writing. i voted in favour of the el khadraoui report on the taxation of heavy goods vehicles for the use of certain infrastructures. it is important to give member states the possibility to apply 'smarter' taxes to the road transport sector to cover external costs and thus encourage greener behaviour. while air and noise pollution must be taken into account, the same cannot be said for congestion not only due to road transport; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the road transport sector is not affected by the introduction of a new road tax. in addition, the sector is paying for the consequences of the economic crisis through the price of oil and the costs of delivering goods. smes in road transport will not be able to bear these additional burdens in the context of the economic crisis. road infrastructure needs to be better adapted to the increase in traffic, but above all, we need to move towards sustainable transport, with a focus on low-carbon modes of transport. as a rhône-alpes elected representative, i can testify to the inadequacy of many road sections in the rhône valley.
in writing. it is remarkable that this report admits several failures of the european union in social matters. first, there is the admission that the objectives of the lisbon strategy will not be achieved in 2010. then there are interesting figures on the increase in the unemployment rate from 7% in 2008 to 8.7% in 2009, more precisely from 7.5% to 9.2% in the euro area, which is a projected loss of 3.5 million jobs. this sad fact should make europeanists reflect on the radical reforms that must be undertaken at member state level in order to limit as far as possible the disastrous effects of the economic and financial crisis, a crisis which has its source in the ultra-liberalism and globalisation so dear to brussels. it is therefore not serious to pursue such a policy of maintaining the guidelines for the employment policies of the member states. on the contrary, we must challenge this managerial logic and give the states back control of their economic and financial resources, while at the same time establishing the national and community preference and protection that will make it possible to regain the internal market and return to growth.
in writing. this own-initiative report should be seen in the context of the current legislative debate to amend the regulations for the structural funds, in particular the erdf regulation (angelakass report) and the esf regulation (jöns report). in order to obtain an agreement at first reading that would allow a rapid response to this crisis that directly affects european citizens, the adle chose not to amend the legislative proposals. for the sake of consistency, the same approach was applied to this vote. my colleagues at modem and i share the same concerns about fighting climate change; this will have to be confirmed as a priority of cohesion policy after 2013.

question a system which has a coherence without accompanying the market players in their definition of an alternative system. that is exactly the difficulty we have in this matter of the exchange committees. the competition directorate has in a number of cases stated that it considers this to be contrary to the competition rules, but then considers that it is up to the industry to find the alternative response. however, the alternative responses that exist at the level of the member states have not been tested by the competition directorate. there is therefore no indication that the competition directorate could support them, nor is there any indication that some of the solutions are appropriate solutions to the problems we are facing. for example, to imagine that the financing of an exchange system could be based on the penalty of the system, that is to say on the errors that would be committed, and therefore very often on the most vulnerable, does not seem to me to be reasonable or socially just. i therefore call on the commission to do two things: to set a deadline for migration and to help define an alternative system or a system acceptable from the point of view of the treaty rules on interchange.

author. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in this long debate which brings us together today, i would like to take a few moments, if you will allow me, to look at the way we have come so far. we remember the first statements by some members of this parliament in the face of growing concern in the acp countries, in the face of anti-pace demonstrations, in the face of the warning signals sent by ngos from the north and the south, when we asked that the priority of these agreements be development, something which would seem almost obvious today, as the commission keeps repeating it. but mr mandelson, at the time, could hardly answer us because, for him, the first thing was to stimulate trade as if the mere opening of customs barriers would bring about the miracle of development. we are being called idealists, we are being called manipulated by ngos, we are being called out for instruments of protection, regulation and intervention by the public authorities. well, it turns out that no, we weren't irresponsible. no, the governments of the acp countries have not accepted that the negotiations should continue under pressure or under threat. no, the risks of opening up trade are not imaginary, they are real and they will have concrete and immediate consequences: reduction of state budgets through loss of customs revenue, weakening of nascent industries in the agricultural sector, risks to the food security of the population. we have expressed these fears long ago, even before the hunger riots or the financial crisis. so what about the situation today? the imf, the world bank and the un all recognise that developing countries, contrary to what was originally stated, will be hit hardest by the global recession. as jacques diouf, director-general of fao, recently pointed out, will we dare to tell those whom we call our partners that we are prepared to spend billions to save the world banking system but not to save their starving populations? i want to be quite frank, commissioner, and i want to make this clear. if you do not make a firm and precise commitment on behalf of the commission to ensure that these epas are genuinely pro-development, i shall not vote for the opinions. i am not going to go into the details of the matter. we want specific commitments and i want to quote them one by one. the epas will only be satisfactory agreements if they promote regional integration, if they contribute to the development of the acp countries and to the achievement of the millennium development goals. when we ask for regional integration to be promoted, this has a concrete meaning. typically, in central africa, cameroon has been singled out, if not strongly criticized, by its neighbours for having signed this interim agreement with the union. i would remind you that five of the eight countries in the region are ldcs, that is to say countries which enjoy, of their own accord and in full compliance with the wto rules, free access to the european market for exports without any counterpart being required from them. i can only understand their concern when the commission asks them to open up to 80% of their exports to europe. so if the commissioner is committed to promoting regional integration, if she is committed to more flexibility to take account of the different levels of development of our partners, can she tell us why she does not accept the offer of 71% liberalisation proposed by central africa? the second key issue on which we are waiting for a response is the singapore issues. these cannot be imposed in the negotiations against the will of the partner countries. i would like to stress this point particularly in relation to public procurement. i will always defend transparency, but can we deprive our acp partners of a key instrument of their sovereignty by supporting their local industry and services by imposing the liberalisation of public procurement? the third point is services. in our epa discussions with cameroon, the commission has repeatedly stressed that our partners want to negotiate on services. maybe this is real. but beware of those who would use this argument to impose the liberalisation of services on all regions and all countries, and especially to justify the liberalisation of public services. commissioner, i expect your firm commitment to keep public services out of the negotiations, in all regions. we know that the loss of customs revenue will cause a decrease in the budgets of our partners. and if incomes fall, the first sectors to suffer will be sectors such as education, health or research. it would therefore be unacceptable in this context for acp governments to lose control of their public services and i call on the commissioner to give us her firm commitment on these matters. fourthly, and this has already been mentioned, food safety must be protected. this means not only providing for adequate safeguards, but also enabling our partners to support their exports in order to remain competitive on world markets. i know that there have been positive developments in this respect in the sadec region. is the commission prepared to propose similar measures in other regions? one last point. we know that the upgrading of the acp economies will require a massive financial commitment from the union both to protect the nascent industries from the negative effects of liberalisation and to develop the competitiveness of our partners' economies. and unfortunately, contrary to the repeated recommendations of our political group, it is the edf funds that will be used as the primary source of funding for the esf. we know that in the past the commission has not been very good at implementing these funds, so i stress the need to use these funds quickly and in accordance with the priorities of our partners. in conclusion, commissioner, these agreements are the image that the european union will give to the rest of the world, the image that the european union will give to the poorest countries of the planet.

in writing. since the introduction of nanoparticles in cosmetic products on the one hand, and the fact that the cosmetics sector is the leading industrial activity for counterfeiting on the other hand, it is important to have clear means of control, in particular to identify counterfeit cosmetic products and therefore, not complying with legal requirements. certain products require special care, such as cosmetics used around the eyes, on mucous membranes, on damaged skin, in children or in people with weakened immune systems. it is clear that particular emphasis should be placed on the assessment of local toxicity, skin and eye irritation, skin sensitisation and, in the case of uv absorption, photo-induced toxicity. moreover, the fight against counterfeiting is imperative through these controls, both in terms of public health, the impact on the environment, but also competitiveness. we shall therefore support this report. however, no further testing of finished products should be carried out if the knowledge of the ingredients contained in the products is in accordance with the standards.
in writing. mr becsey's report proposes further harmonisation and a higher level of taxation on tobacco and is loosely based on public health objectives to justify this. the real objective is a pure and perfect cigarette market at european level, a 'closed' market with a single taxation system, where competition can play out to the full. a little consistency ! either health comes first, or the market. for some products, it cannot be the market. some countries, such as france and belgium, are being sued by the commission for having introduced threshold prices, minimum selling prices. and it is not without reason that the tobacco trade is so heavily regulated, at national level (distribution subject to authorization) or international (limited cross-border purchases) and that for once, border controls actually exist, even if they are hampered by european regulations. finally, the report raises concerns about the future of french farmers, who play such an important role in maintaining local shops and the provision of certain public services in rural areas, and who had been seriously jeopardised by a previous tax increase.

the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs has adopted a recommendation for second reading on the common consular instructions: biometric identification and visa applications (05329/1/2009 - c6-0088/2009 - 2006/0088 ((cod)) rapporteur: sarah ludford (a6-0143/2009)
on behalf of the pse group. madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, you are chairing this sitting and it is therefore your place to speak on this matter which you have followed as rapporteur for an opinion. first of all, i would like to warmly congratulate sarah ludford on the energy and results she has brought to bear in the difficult negotiation of this dossier. i think the european parliament can be proud of the results achieved because the task was far from easy, as we have seen. i would like to stress two points in particular which i consider essential and on which we can be particularly satisfied. first, the raising of the age limit for fingerprinting of minors from six to twelve years; the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of personal data in the event of a breach of the rights of the individual. i know that some people feel that the solution adopted does not fully fit in with the options we have proposed, particularly as regards the collection by a service provider in a diplomatic office and the transfer of data by encrypted e-mail or even by encrypted electronic media carried in a diplomatic bag. it should be noted, however, that the collection by private bodies can only be done in compliance with european legislation and that the data must be fully encrypted by the provider and transmitted to the authorities of the member state. in addition, we have been given the reference to the need to negotiate agreements with third countries which prohibit the encryption of data transmitted electronically. the examination of applications, any interviews, the authorisation procedure and the printing and affixing of visa sticker will be carried out solely by the diplomatic or consular representation. the same conditions apply to the transmission of data collected from one member state to another in the case of colocalisations, i.e. the representation of one member state by another in a third country. finally, if the detailed conditions for the activity of service providers are described in an annex to the text, they will have to be defined in a binding legal framework. in view of these results, we can only welcome the guarantees thus obtained in the direction of a better visa policy in europe, which will certainly benefit european citizens and improve our relations with third countries.

europe set out a road map for the g20 meeting on 2 april, after having, from the beginning of the crisis, drawn our american partners and the rest of the world into an ambitious and very necessary in writing. i voted in favour of this recommendation, put forward by the british democrat sarah ludford, on common consular instructions: biometric identification and visa applications. the agreement at second reading confirms the intention to introduce biometric data into the european visa information system (vis). the common consular instructions also ensure that all member states issue visas to nationals of nearly 100 countries, on the basis of similar criteria and characteristics. the text thus has the merit of introducing fundamental measures for the protection of citizens, as well as provisions ensuring respect for the privacy and personal data of third-country nationals.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the performance and sustainability of the european aeronautical system, presented by my romanian colleague marian-jean marinescu. the text is part of the single sky ii package and aims to improve the performance of the european aeronautical system. it addresses several concerns: environmental concerns, through the introduction of measures to reduce co2 emissions; functional concerns, since it aims to streamline air traffic by increasing capacity and optimum route planning; and concerns about the safety of european citizens, by encouraging cooperation and coordination between the various actors. following the single sky i package, this report has the merit of presenting a dynamic vision of the current challenges by proposing long-term solutions for an effective modernisation of the aviation sector.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we did not vote on any of the texts on the new partnership agreements with the poorest acp countries in the world. we are not voting against these countries, which deserve a genuine policy of cooperation and development that helps them to lift their populations out of poverty, their territories out of underdevelopment and their economies out of difficulties. they also deserve trade relations which take account of their particular situations, but also of our own interests, and in particular those of our outermost regions, which are forgotten in your policies. what you are proposing to them are agreements which are in accordance with the sacrosanct rules of the wto, and which are designed to insert them into ultra-liberal globalisation. you condemn them to export crops that starve them and to the exploitation of their wealth by multinational companies which have long ceased to serve a particular country but are stateless, anonymous and motivated only by their financial interests. these countries have the right to choose the pace of opening their borders and liberalising their economies. and why not take another path, that of reasonable protectionism and mutually beneficial relations, based on reciprocity. this is the path we are also asking for france and europe.
in writing. according to the epas, sugar and bananas from acp countries will not be able to access the markets of the french outermost regions (ors) for a renewable period of ten years, thus preserving the production of these two pillars of overseas agriculture. the specific safeguard clause, which allows imports to be blocked in the event of injury or disturbance to the oct market, should be further specified in order to reduce the time taken for its implementation. the calls made by parliament have therefore made it possible to take account of the demands of the ors in the negotiations. overseas socio-professional actors feel that they are penalized by production constraints that respect european standards, making them less competitive than their direct competitors. i understand them, but i nevertheless encourage them to engage fully in a process of cooperation with their acp neighbours, in order to foster complementarities and solidarity on commonly defined objectives. rather than camping on a defensive position, the rup have every advantage in positioning themselves in a competition of equals. the european union must provide adequate means of control and arbitration to avoid any form of unfair competition.
in writing. for years, alongside our african colleagues, socialists have been mobilizing to make the epas real instruments of development. we have negotiated with the commission with strength and determination to achieve fair agreements in the service of the millennium development goals. by playing the card of regionalization chosen and conducted by the acp themselves. by keeping our commitments on trade aid promised in 2005 rather than continuing to "plunder" the edf. today our fight has largely paid off, as the trade commissioner has committed herself on behalf of the european commission to: - the essential objective of developing the agreements; - the renegotiation of the disputed points of the agreements in an open and flexible approach; - food security and the protection of the fragile industries of the acp countries. of course we would have liked more guarantees on the involvement of national parliaments and the acp-eu assembly in monitoring the implementation of the agreements. but within a few weeks, the progress is considerable. i'll take that under advisement. but i want to be very vigilant about their implementation. so no white-seing, abstention is the rule.
in writing. our position on the economic partnership agreements is still critical. we believe that the negotiations have started very badly, by not respecting the specificities of our partners. we are also convinced that negotiations with them should not be rushed and, above all, that they should not be forced to implement abrupt reforms which could prove disastrous for their social cohesion and their economies. but our vote takes account of the very encouraging statements made by commissioner ashton in the plenary on monday 23 march. that is why we abstained and did not vote against, as we would certainly have done a few weeks ago. however, our abstention is a warning: we want to judge the commission's action on the basis of facts and do not want to give it a blank check for the future.
in writing. i voted in favour of this joint resolution on the future of the motor industry. the text emphasises the need for a clear and coherent policy at european level to deal with a crisis affecting all eu member states. it is estimated that 12 million jobs in europe are directly or indirectly linked to the automobile industry. sales are falling, stocks are increasing, there are more and more redundancies: in the face of the social disaster that is looming, there is no miracle, only coordinated measures can save the sector. that is why i voted in favour of this joint resolution which calls on the european authorities, in conjunction with the member states, to put in place measures to ensure the future competitiveness of the european automobile industry and the sustainability of employment in the european automobile sector. the resolution, however, comes a little late and does not meet all expectations. the debate is therefore far from over and promises to be heated, especially in view of the current social challenges and the reaffirmed need for a social europe that protects its citizens.
in writing. we voted on the resolution on the automobile industry. but we must not forget that those who today pretend to save it are the real ones responsible for this disaster. they are responsible for the expansion of a financialized, global economy, disconnected from reality, where the guarantee of high returns for shareholders takes the place of industrial strategy, where shares rise with the announcement of social plans, while bosses who are not always capable are awarded bonuses and golden parachutes. they created this system where the employment and the wages of the workers became the only adjustment variables. they are responsible for the impoverishment of households which weighs heavily on demand, fuelling the vicious circle. even now, when hundreds of thousands of jobs are at stake, the commission is raising the dogma of competition, impeding national measures to avoid job losses, holding renault to account to ensure that the increase in production in a factory is not the result of a relocation of activity. i am not sure that the commissioner has been able to give us a clear answer to this question. it's time to change policy. for the good of europe and especially of europeans.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i am speaking on behalf of our colleague, mr jacques toubon. i would first like to thank our colleague, mr popa, who has done an excellent job of trying to find compromises acceptable to all, despite the extreme positions taken by some of my colleagues in the pse and the greens on this issue. the report raises the important question of the balance between security and fundamental freedoms on the internet. while many people see this new technology as a symbol of progress and opportunity, it is not without its dangers. for example, it is essential to ensure freedom of expression and information on this new medium, while ensuring that this is done in harmony with respect for other fundamental freedoms, such as the protection of privacy, personal data and respect for intellectual property. the rapporteur, mr lambrinidis, has done an excellent job in taking account of the new forms of crime on the internet and the dangers it poses, particularly to minors. unfortunately, the report is more ambiguous and even dangerous in other respects. the amendments tabled by our colleagues hieronymi, mavrommatis and jacques toubon are intended to make it clear that infringements of fundamental freedoms should not be condoned in the name of freedom of expression and information. member states and internet actors should retain some leeway to find the best solutions so that the rights of some do not radically impede the exercise of the rights of others. laws should apply on the internet as they apply everywhere else. the internet cannot be a virtual territory where an act that constitutes a legal offence in the real world would be considered authorized, and even protected by the mere effect of the technology and the use made of it. the rule of law in our democratic societies is at stake.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, as an artist i am sorry, i am very shocked by the lack of interest in the cultural sector in mr lambrinidis' report. i would stress that the rights of individuals must be safeguarded and protected at all times, in accordance with the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, and that the rights and freedoms of all parties concerned must be guaranteed. the information society is an increasingly important economic sector, but also a major source of innovation and creativity, which underpins the modern economy. this includes ensuring access for all to a diverse culture and education in a context that respects community law and the fair recognition of the value of the creative work of authors and performers, including in the digital economy. this recognition implies remuneration for their creative contribution to all types of use so that they can live and work independently in their profession. in this context, intellectual property rights should not be seen as a barrier but rather as a driver of creative activities, particularly in the context of the development of new online services. on the other hand, i believe that even on the internet racist, hateful or negative speech should be subject to criminal prosecution. freedom of expression must be exercised responsibly. a balance needs to be struck between free access to the internet, respect for privacy and protection of intellectual property. i therefore ask you, ladies and gentlemen, to support my amendments nos 2 to 6.
madam president, madam commissioner, the lisbon strategy is a great success in at least one respect. the european union has become one of the most competitive areas in the world in terms of poverty manufacturing. we have thus been able to provide 80 million poor people and 43 million hungry europeans, including the elderly, who may die sooner and thus reduce public expenditure, thus better meeting the maastricht criteria. in france alone, we have 80 million meals served, every year, by restos du coeur. to feed these poor people since 1987, we had a food distribution programme, a budget of 300 million euros a year. 300 million divided by 80, divided by 12, that's enough to distribute 25 cents of food a month to each of the 80 million poor. this food was taken from intervention stocks but since the 1992 reform, when the butter mountains, the milk rivers, the refrigerators that were overflowing were criticized, these stocks have been exhausted. and for 2010-12, we will buy foodstuffs on the market, where non-european products also arrive, in the name of the wto and the fight against protectionism. that is to say, since 1962 we have been feeding our cattle with imported oilseeds, and from 2010 we will feed our poor, here too, with imports. all this, co-financed in the name of universality. but the problem, madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the real problem is that there are still 80 million poor people after 22 years of food programmes.

in writing. it is clear that there is currently little reliable and accepted scientific data on the effects of magnetic fields on the human body. yet these objects are part of our daily lives (mobile phones, wireless technologies) and 80% of citizens feel that they are not sufficiently informed about these potential effects, and 50% of them say they are concerned. so far, the scientific community has been able to express only divided and sometimes contradictory opinions, and the public authorities have not really addressed this problem. i therefore wholeheartedly support this report which calls on the member states to update the threshold values for these fields regularly and which recommends, in accordance with the precautionary principle, that antennas be banned from being installed in risk areas (schools, health institutions). i also support the european commission launching a scientific study to better assess the effects of exposure to electromagnetic fields. public authorities, industry and consumers need to be given accurate information to measure these risks and, if necessary, to take appropriate protective measures. it is also important to formulate recommendations, based on good practice, to better protect the health of citizens, whether they are users of equipment or near relay antennas or high voltage lines.

mr president, multilingual education, polyglot teachers who speak to each child in his or her mother tongue, foreign teachers recruited specifically for them, respect for and even appreciation of the cultures of origin by the school, a minimum knowledge of the language of the host country, not even considered as truly compulsory, this type of recipe does not lead to the integration of migrants. it also leads, paradoxically, to the communitarianisation of our societies, the blurring of identities, the acculturation of all, both migrants and the indigenous inhabitants of the host country. i would advise the rapporteur to look in the zeps - the french suburban priority education areas - where this kind of good feeling is leading, which in fact only manifests the refusal to impose respect for our own cultures, customs and morals in our own countries on those who come to ask for hospitality. our education systems don't have to adapt to other cultures. it is up to the migrant populations to adapt to our cultures if they wish to remain in our countries.
mr president, the ancient greeks had already discussed the issues we are dealing with. in their city associations, they discussed the respective merits of isopoliteia, or identical citizenship, which gave everyone the same rights from one city to another, or sympoliteia, or common citizenship. it will not surprise you that i am strongly in favour of the first of these provisions. european citizenship is largely artificial. the rapporteur regrets above all the lack of awareness among citizens of the rights which it can grant them. but i have noticed that when we ask these citizens what they think, for example about the european constitution or its illegible avatar, the treaty of lisbon, and they say no, then their views are deliberately ignored. that is why these supposedly generous constructions of common citizenship seem to me to be largely hypocritical and i would prefer to replace them with mutual recognition of rights between allied but still sovereign nations.
mr president, the great catholic philosopher chesterton said that the modern world was full of christian ideas that had gone mad. i think the buitenweg report is a perfect example of this. it is a text which starts with good feelings in order to avoid discrimination which could be suffered by, for example, disabled people, and which reaches a true totalitarianism by making a fundamental conceptual error, that is, by failing to distinguish between legitimate differences and discrimination which is unjust. for example, it is natural for a child to have a father and a mother, even if he is adopted. this right must prevail over the right of persons of the same sex to adopt a child. it is natural that there should be distinctions based on nationality. it is natural that the french at home, the british at home, the czechs, the lithuanians are preferred in their own countries to foreigners, just as it is natural that these foreigners are preferred in their own countries to european citizens. these are perfectly legitimate distinctions, which are ignored in this text, which, moreover, destroys the presumption of innocence. this new doctrine of political correctness is a real step towards soft totalitarianism.
mr president, it is indeed a good thing that national socialism is being put on the same footing as communism and included in a general condemnation of the totalitarianisms which bled the 20th century and which, however, were very much in favour of many intellectuals, who were never asked to account and many of whom, moreover, sit in the most prominent positions among these ranks. it is good that a number of amendments which tended to pollute this text have been withdrawn. i do not think, however, that one can, for example, attach an absolutely irrefutable value to the official history of this dark period of our history, nor condemn heterodox minds. it is absolutely astonishing that in france it is a law of communist inspiration, the guessot law, which still frames the historical debate under heavy criminal sanctions. our colleague jacques toubon called it stalinist when it was adopted. well, his friend, mr barrot, the justice commissioner, proposes to extend it to all the countries of the union which do not have it and even to triple the penalties and prison sentences that go with it. it is not with totalitarian methods that one can fight totalitarianism.
mr president, i voted in favour of mrs ries' report on the concerns about the health effects of electromagnetic fields. electromagnetic fields do exist in nature, but the demand for electricity and especially the development of wireless technologies have led to a rapid increase in the exposure of citizens to electromagnetic waves. we must therefore be vigilant, and the european parliament has understood this. as the member for the north-west constituency in france, i can testify to the danger posed by certain very high voltage power lines installed in my constituency, near schools and health facilities, particularly those in the french department of la manche, which put local workers and residents at high risk of exposure to the waves emitted. since scientists disagree on the consequences of electromagnetic fields for the health of our fellow citizens, it is appropriate to be responsible and to apply the precautionary principle. the limit values should therefore be updated regularly in order to ensure an adequate level of protection for citizens. the european parliament has here drawn the attention of the european commission to this matter which rightly concerns the citizens. the european union must do more in this area by establishing a clear policy on electromagnetic waves, by providing more information to citizens on this issue and by adopting binding community legislation.
in writing. every child has the right to education. the integration of migrants, whether they are in a regular or irregular situation, is a priority for us socialists. we do not accept the hierarchy that the right wing in parliament wants to create between migrants. that is why i abstained on the excellent takkula report on the education of migrant children because, as an own-initiative report, we were not able to put forward separate votes to ask for the deletion of paragraphs 5, 8 and 16 which i am absolutely not satisfied with. it is through the education of migrant children that we will make a strong contribution to the integration of all, regardless of their status. it is by creating favourable socioeconomic conditions that we can best help migrants, whether they are legally resident in europe, whether they are destined to be regularised or whether they are finally returning to their countries. we cannot create a status of non-education and ghettoization for children simply because their parents are in an irregular situation. this is clearly contrary to international conventions.

in writing. the report by mr gacek on citizenship of the union is a complete fraud. under the guise of strengthening the freedom of movement and residence of community nationals in the european union, it establishes genuine equality of treatment between community nationals and third-country nationals. the report deliberately uses the general term 'citizenship', which unlawfully encompasses the concepts of nationality of a member state and citizenship of the union. the objective, beyond the deliberate confusion, is very clear: to extend the possibility of acquiring the nationality of a member state to any person legally residing in that state under the secondary right of citizenship of the union. the rapporteur therefore introduces a new concept of intra-community migrant, a species in the process of multiplying. it is true that the european parliament is now made up of representatives of the citizens of the union and no longer of the peoples of the member states. it is a serious attack on national identity and cohesion. beware, ladies and gentlemen, as representatives of the undifferentiated citizens of the european union, you will soon become stateless members of parliament. but deep down, that may be what you want.
in writing. the defence of the rights and protection of persons who are victims of discrimination must be a priority for the eu, but it can only be effective and useful if it provides legal certainty for the persons concerned while avoiding a disproportionate burden for the economic actors concerned. in this sensitive area, it was essential to remain vigilant about respecting the division of competences between the european union and the member states and to ensure that parliament strictly adheres to what the legal basis allows. the text as adopted today, while satisfactory in some respects - particularly as regards the fight against discrimination against disabled people - contains vague concepts, legal uncertainties and superfluous requirements which make it legally impracticable and therefore ineffective in its application. i believe that over-regulation cannot be a solution and i have therefore supported the amendment rejecting the commission's proposal, since the existing texts on this subject are not being applied by a number of member states which are the subject of infringement proceedings. in these circumstances, i was in favour of the objective of this directive but was partially dissatisfied, and i chose to abstain in the final vote.

in writing. since 2000, the european union has been promoting equality in the widest possible sense: equality between men and women, between nationals and foreigners, between the sick and the healthy, between catholics, muslims, buddhists and other religions, equality in access to education, health, sexual orientation, etc. in short, the list is obviously not exhaustive and the next european directives in preparation concern equality in access to social services and housing. this is a new directive which, under the guise of a legitimate fight against discrimination against disabled people, intends to regulate, if not to lock up, practically all areas where freedom of choice, contractual or otherwise, still exists. the pitfalls of such coercive regulation are many. these new european measures will not only increase bureaucracy and european burdens, but they also represent a real danger to other freedoms and fundamental rights, such as freedom of religion, association or expression and freedom of the press. in the name of equality, censors and dictators are here.

in writing. i voted in favour of the ries report on the concerns about the health effects of electromagnetic fields. it is essential to ensure a high level of consumer protection, and in particular that of children, without hampering the operation of mobile telephone networks. although there is no scientific evidence to show that the use of mobile phones poses a health risk, this hypothesis cannot be definitively excluded and it is therefore necessary that this issue be included in the framework of the precautionary principle. it is important to update the limit values for the exposure of the public to electromagnetic fields regularly. finally, there is an urgent need for more information on the effects of electromagnetic waves and for a single system of authorizations for the installation of antennas and relays, as the report stresses.
in writing. schools are a fundamental issue that needs to be reaffirmed today. the report entitled 'improving schools: a programme of european cooperation', which i fully supported, is part of this objective. it stresses in particular the need to guarantee equal access for all young european citizens to quality education, enabling the acquisition of sound skills and knowledge. it also called for more financial support for schools in difficulty. alongside basic knowledge, the resolution also rightly stresses the importance of learning foreign languages from an early age, as well as the opportunity to receive artistic, cultural and physical education, which are essential for personal development. it also recommends greater mobility and exchanges in the school environment and cites the excellent european comenius programme in this respect, noting, however, the need to make it more visible and more accessible. the resolution also encourages, in strict compliance with the principle of subsidiarity, the establishment of modernised school curricula taking account of technological developments and the opportunities they offer.

on behalf of the alde group. madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, in september 2007 the european commission presented its third energy package on the functioning of the internal market. the debate soon turned to the important but not unique question of the separation of energy production and transmission. the question of ownership of networks, which was not sufficiently addressed in my view at first reading, seems to have been taken more seriously. the coexistence of different options, including the famous third way, strengthened and clarified, seems to me to be a good thing, which is obvious because i was a co-author of this amendment. but, fortunately, to reduce this third package to ownership unbundling would be a mistake. the advances are real: more rights for consumers, more power for regulators, more cooperation between regulators, 10-year investment plans, more transparency to facilitate the development of renewables, more technical cooperation between grid operators, and also tools to consume better, such as smart meters. this is a new step towards european solidarity. the 'third country' clause, although it seems less sensational than the one originally drafted by the commission, explicitly states that a member state has the right to refuse certification to an operator if this endangers the security of its energy supply or the security of supply of another member state. perhaps a regret about the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators; we would have liked to have created a strong, independent agency, capable of making decisions without the approval of our body. we bumped into each other at the famous meroni stop. let us not be fooled: the construction of a genuine european energy policy will still require many advances, particularly institutional ones. security of supply, the fight against climate change, market regulation - all these objectives should be pursued in a pragmatic and not dogmatic approach. what european citizens want is not the application of economic theories but concrete evidence that open markets bring benefits: freedom to choose their supplier, reasonable, stable and predictable prices. i thank my colleagues, our dear commissioner and the council for this constructive work.
the rapporteur. - mr president, mr vice-president and mr kallas, ladies and gentlemen, my first words are to thank you, mr vice-president kallas, and your colleagues from the commission for the attention you have paid to the parliamentary work on the discharge procedure for the implementation of the 2007 budget of the european commission and the executive agencies. i would like to thank the administration for their support. i would also like to commend the immense work done by the european court of auditors under the leadership of its president, vítor caldeira, with limited resources in view of the scale of the task to be accomplished. a few words about the context of this dump. 2007 is the first year of the new multiannual financial framework 2007-13 in which many new rules have been implemented. 2007 was also the last discharge procedure for the present commission, which, at the beginning of its mandate, had promised - you remember, commissioner, through your president - to obtain a positive declaration of assurance from the european court of auditors. for the last 14 years, the court has issued a negative declaration on the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions for the vast majority of expenditure, considering it to be affected to varying degrees by significant errors, even though, fortunately, the consolidated accounts and administrative expenditure are the subject of a positive declaration of assurance. finally, 2007 is the last discharge vote before the european parliament elections. in this particular context, and beyond the many reservations on the management of community funds contained in the draft resolution, i wanted to try, through my report, to analyse the discharge procedure and to make a contribution to the difficult path which must lead us to a positive declaration of assurance, while being well aware of the limit of the year. and that is why i look forward to hearing the commission's position, the political groups and my colleagues in parliament. at the end of the work on this matter, i have a mixed feeling between the conviction that things are improving, but not enough and too slowly, and the fact that, at the same time, it is not tenable to remain in a situation where, for fourteen years, the european court of auditors has not given positive assurance and where the european parliament still votes on discharge. the citizen will come to believe that parliament is not fulfilling its role of control properly. i therefore propose, in view of the seriousness of the situation, that an interinstitutional conference be held as soon as possible, involving all those involved in the management and control of community funds, in order to begin a comprehensive discussion on the reforms needed to obtain a positive declaration of assurance as soon as possible. i look forward to hearing the reasons why certain political groups oppose this approach. particular attention should also be paid to the role of the member states, which manage about 80% of the union budget. it is in this shared management that we have the greatest problems. in this respect, i regret that the council is empty, and the current political difficulties in the czech republic are not sufficient to explain why there is no continuity in the political presence of the council, except to interpret this absence and silence as indifference, or worse, disinterest. as regards the report on shared management by the member states, i would stress the role of national management declarations, but also the role of the annual audit summaries, which are all elements that can help to achieve a positive sda. in addition, and in accordance with article 248 of the treaty, i propose that cooperation between the national audit institutions and the european court of auditors be stepped up in the area of shared management. i suggest that consideration be given to the issue by the national audit institutions, as independent external auditors and in compliance with international auditing standards, of national audit certificates on the management of community funds which would be provided to the governments of the member states for production under the discharge process in accordance with an appropriate interinstitutional procedure to be set up. finally, mr president, i would like to stress my surprise at the fact that the consolidated annual accounts are presented with negative equity capital of eur 58 billion, and i suggest that consideration be given to the creation of a pension fund to outsource the eur 33.5 billion of liabilities to staff. i conclude by saying that i believe it is time to reform our system, and i sincerely believe that this reform must be achieved through a thorough and sincere dialogue between all the budgetary actors.
mr president, in this period of economic recession it was important that the european union should continue to show solidarity with the developing countries. in 2007, the european community and its member states together contributed 60% of total development aid, making the eu the world's largest donor. the european development funds help to combat poverty, while promoting economic development and democracy. i am therefore pleased that the acp countries have been allocated a budget of eur 23 billion for the period 2008-2013 under the 10th edf, which is almost double the amount foreseen for the 9th edf. the court of auditors concluded in its report that the accounts of the seventh, eighth and ninth edfs were, in general, fair, legal and regular. the record levels of contract execution and payments from the edf implementation are to be welcomed. however, i also note that further progress is still needed to strengthen the control and monitoring mechanism as there is still a significant level of error affecting certain transactions. similarly, there is too often a high risk in budget support and i think that there is a need to assess these risks better. in this respect, i share the view that budget support should only be granted if the recipient country has the capacity to manage the funds in a transparent, accountable and efficient manner. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the financing of the european development fund is a very good one. in conclusion, mr president, i would like to thank the rapporteur for his excellent report, the representatives of the court, but also all the commission staff who did an excellent job on the spot, and i regret, of course, the absence of the council, and in particular of the czech presidency.
the rapporteur. - mr president, i think the case of romania and bulgaria deserves to be discussed, but we are really in an extremely serious situation. i would like to thank the rapporteurs of the political groups, all the speakers, and in particular the committee on budgetary control, for their conclusions, and i would like to conclude on a number of points. firstly, in the budget we have no fraud. secondly, we have a lot of errors, and we have a lot of errors for two reasons: firstly, our regulations are too complex and, as a result, the final beneficiaries have a lot of difficulty applying too complex regulations and make mistakes that are not so serious. and the second reason is that the european court of auditors applies a very low threshold of 2% for all sectors. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject. so, things go wrong, we say, but because we're all responsible. the commission is responsible for not keeping its promise and thank you, commissioner, for taking stock of the proposals for the next mandate. the council is responsible because it is not interested: it is not there. the member states are responsible because they apply the regulations with insufficient rigour. the european court of auditors is responsible because it has to ask questions about its audit methods, and in particular about the rates of service; it is up to the commission, not the commission or parliament, to set the thresholds of significance. parliament is responsible because it must be clear about the current imperfections and accept the reforms. in short, i think we have a set of shared responsibilities. the synthesis is made at the end of this term. we hope that this reform will be carried out so that in the next financial perspective we will finally have a positive declaration of assurance and, if we have a negative declaration of assurance, we will have a negative vote in parliament, so that there will be political consistency between the bodies which have to decide on budgetary control.

the continuing development of the european union, namely a common immigration policy. as indicated in the report itself, the immigration pact adopted by the european council last year served as a new impetus for a common policy in the area of immigration and asylum. we now need to ensure that the commitments outlined in this plan are put into effect. the commission will next month propose means of monitoring the implementation of this pact by means of annual reports by the commission. these reports serve to prepare an annual debate in the european council on immigration and asylum policy with effect from the year 2010. the definition of the general objectives of the common policy as set out in this pact will continue to be drawn up in a multiannual programme, namely the stockholm programme to be adopted later this year under the swedish presidency. the busuttil report provides the commission with very useful material for the contribution that the commission intends to make by means of a communication to be adopted before next summer. i would like to emphasise the general convergence of our ideas. in several parts where the busuttil report calls on the commission to take action, i would like to say that the commission has already engaged actively, for example, in relation to the development of facilities for temporary and circular immigration, improving the collection and system as a step to promoting ownership and responsibility of candidate countries and potential candidates. guidance and assistance is being given to them in order for these countries to build the required public management structures and public financial control systems. according to the principles of ipa, environmental protection, good governance, civil society development, gender equality and non-discrimination are all cross-cutting issues and are an integral part of project design. civil society organisations are now more actively involved in the development and the initiation of projects. in 2008 the commission launched the civil society facility as a tool for promoting civil society development and advancement of regional cooperation, for which an indicative budget of eur 130 million is earmarked for 2008-2010. the commission also shares the rapporteur’s views as regards the importance of education, regional and cross-border cooperation and gender equality, to name but the agenda calls for a brief presentation of the report by neena gill, on behalf of the committee on legal affairs, on the effective enforcement of judicial decisions in the european union: transparency of debtors' assets (2008/2233) (ini)) (a6-0252/2009).
member of the commission. − mr president, i am very pleased to have this opportunity to discuss parliament’s concerns regarding the issue of debt recovery abroad. i would also like to thank ms gill for the report. what is at stake? both parliament and the commission agree that the problems of cross-border debt recovery may constitute a serious obstacle to the free circulation of payment orders within the european union and may impede access to justice. furthermore, this is key for the survival of small businesses in the current economic climate. against this background and in accordance with the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, what should be the community objectives? the european union has an impressive set of legal measures to ensure access to justice in cross-border cases and to facilitate the free circulation of civil and commercial decisions within the union. however, there is no doubt – as stated in the hague programme on mutual recognition adopted by the european council – that it would in fact be much easier to enforce judgments within the european union if it were possible to obtain accurate information on debtors’ financial positions. the commission published a green paper on the transparency of debtors’ assets in march 2008, and all the replies – including a summary – can now be accessed by consulting the public web site. most of the respondents agreed with the need for measures at community level to increase the transparency of debtors’ assets, though views differ as to what can be done in practice. i am grateful to parliament for presenting such a detailed response to the green paper. the report is rather sceptical of the ideas put forward in the green paper, believing that the main problem is that of recalcitrant debtors who are unscrupulous. the report is also very concerned about the data-protection/privacy issues related to obtaining information about people’s financial situation. the commission is also committed to protecting privacy and the personal data of citizens. the report instead calls for the adoption of national directories of foreign lawyers working in other member staes as a way to help creditors and suggests a community provisional measure. i would like to inform parliament that improving the practical enforcement of judgments will be a high priority of the commission in the future stockholm programme in the area of justice, freedom and security for the period 2010-2014 that the commission will present in 2009. however, the commission has not yet programmed any specific legislative measure in terms of follow-up to its green paper. finally, in the light of the first results of the consultation, the commission believes that this proposal – that is, to draw up a manual of national enforcement laws, to increase access to commercial and public registers, to improve cooperation between enforcement authorities and to create a compulsory assets declaration by the debtor – will go some way towards fulfilling our objectives. in this respect, of course, careful consideration will be given by the commission to parliament’s resolution on the different issues incorporated in this report.
the point is closed. the vote will take place on wednesday 22 april 2009.
